H. TAT Probe Installation
NOTE: The following procedure is for installing an aspirated TAT probe in airplanes configured for
an aspirated TAT probe, and for installing non-aspirated TAT probe in airplanes configured
for non-aspirated TAT probe.
SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-002
(1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3
Row Col Number Name
C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE
SUBTASK 34-21-06-110-001
(2) Clean and prepare the surface and sides of the installation hole, do this task: Clean Bare,
Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent, TASK 20-10-34-110-802.
SUBTASK 34-21-06-420-001
(3) Do these steps to install the TAT probe [4]:
34-21-06
(a) Put the new gasket [2] into its position on the TAT probe [4].
NOTE: It is not necessary to fit a new gasket if acquiring one will cause a flight delay.
The old gasket, if in good condition, can be reused and replaced with a new
gasket in one week or less.
(b) Remove the protective cap from the electrical connector [1].
(c) Examine the electrical connector [1] for loose, bent, or broken pins.
(d) Connect the electrical connector [1] to the TAT probe [4].
(e) Carefully put the TAT probe [4] into its position.
NOTE: The large intake must point forward.
1) Make sure that remove caps and examine pins before installation.
(f) Install the screws [3] that hold the TAT probe [4] to the airplane.
(g) Tighten the screws [3] to 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m) - 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m).
SUBTASK 34-21-06-760-001
(4) Do these steps to complete the bonding measurement check:
(a) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and
airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less.
(b) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm), do these steps:
1) Remove the TAT probe [4].
2) Clean the bonding surfaces, including the countersunk holes in the TAT probe [4]
(SWPM 20-20-00).
3) Replace the screws [3] with new screws [3].
4) Install the TAT probe [4].
5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4]
and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00).
a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
b) Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less.
6) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm), do these steps:
a) Remove the TAT probe [4].
b) Replace the nutplates and rivets that attach the TAT probe [4] (SRM
51-40-02).
c) Install the TAT probe [4].
d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT
probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00).
<1> Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614.
<2> Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less.
34-21-06
SUBTASK 34-21-06-390-001
(5) Apply sealant, A00247, around the TAT probe [4].
NOTE: It is not necessary to apply the sealant immediately, if the cure time will cause a flight
delay. But, you must apply the sealant as soon as possible to keep moisture out of the
area between the probe and airplane skin. The sealant must not wait more than a
maximum of eight weeks to apply.
SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-003
(6) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3
Row Col Number Name
C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE

J. TAT System Test
SUBTASK 34-21-06-730-001
(1) Do this task: Pitot Probe, AOA Sensor, and TAT Probe Heater - System Test,
TASK 30-31-00-730-801.
SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-005
(2) Do these steps to get access the Air Data Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) maintenance
index on the Control Display Unit (CDU):
NOTE: CDU data lines that permit a selection are identified with a caret (< or >). The CDU has
12 line-select-keys. Six keys are on each side of the display. 1L thru 6L are on the left
side, and 1R thru 6R are on the right side.
(a) Push the INIT REF key.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the INIT REF INDEX 1/1 page.
(b) Push the LSK 6R adjacent to the MAINT> prompt on the CDU.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page.
(c) Push the LSK 4L adjacent to the <ADIRS prompt on the CDU.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS BITE 1/1 page.
SUBTASK 34-21-06-710-002
(3) Do these steps to get access the left ADIRS current faults:
(a) Set the IRS MSU left mode select switch to NAV position.
(b) Push the LSK 1L adjacent to the <ADIRS L prompt on the CDU.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS L BITE MAIN MENU page.
(c) Push the LSK 1L adjacent to the <CURRENT STATUS prompt on the CDU.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS L BITE CURRENT FAULTS page.
2) Make sure that the CDU does not show the TAT PROBE SIGNAL FAIL message.
NOTE: If there is a maintenance message that shows on the CDU, you can go to
the ADIRS fault isolation procedures to repair the fault
FIM 34-21 TASK 813.
SUBTASK 34-21-06-710-003
(4) Do these steps to access the right ADIRS current faults.
(a) Set the IRS MSU right mode select switch to NAV position.
(b) Push the LSK 2L adjacent to the <ADIRS R prompt on the CDU from the ADIRS BITE 1/1
page.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS R BITE MAIN MENU page.
(c) Push the LSK 1L adjacent to the <CURRENT STATUS prompt on the CDU.
1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS R BITE CURRENT FAULTS page.
34-21-06
2) Make sure that the CDU does not show the TAT PROBE SIGNAL FAIL message.
NOTE: If there is a maintenance message that shows on the CDU, you can go to
the ADIRS fault isolation procedure to fix the fault FIM 34-21 TASK 813.

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 34-21-06-200-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE TAT PROBE HEAT IS OFF . THE PROBE BECOMES
HOT IF IT IS ON. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(1) Visually examine the Total Air T emperature (TAT) probe of the air inlet scoop and air exit ports
for blockages caused by unwanted material.
(a) Make sure that air passes freely through the tube.
1) If there is unwanted material, contamination, or Foreign Object Debris (FOD), then
replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
(2) Visually examine the sensor for physical damage such as cracking or separation of parts on
the air scoop and strut.
(a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
34-21-06
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ASPIRATED TAT PROBES
(3) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.17 in. (4.32 mm) deep, measured from the
leading edge of the strut. When measuring from the trailing edge of the strut, any
measurement less than 1.83 in. (46.48 mm) is unacceptable.
(a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH NON-ASPIRATED TAT PROBES
(4) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.08 in. (2.03 mm) deep, measured from the
leading edge of the strut. When measuring from the trailing edge of the strut, any
measurement less than 1.57 in. (39.88 mm) is unacceptable.
(a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ASPIRATED TAT PROBES
(5) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.04 in. (1.02 mm) deep, measured from the
front of scoop. When measuring from back of scoop, any measurement less than 2.11 in.
(53.59 mm) is unacceptable.
(a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
RYR ALL; AIRPLANES WITH NON-ASPIRATED TAT PROBES
(6) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.04 in. (1.02 mm) deep, measured from the
front of scoop. When measuring from back of scoop, any measurement less than 3.46 in.
(87.88 mm) is unacceptable.
(a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
(7) Visually check the interior of the air scoop to see if the airbump has worn away. The sensor is
serviceable regardless of condition of airbump as long as it is present.
(a) If the airbump has worn away, then replace the TAT probe.
These are the tasks:
Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801
Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801
RYR ALL
34-21-06

E. Standby Compass Calibrator (SCC) Adjustment
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-001
(1) Calibrate the Standby Compass Calibrator (SCC) (standby compass calibration kit,
COM-1925) to the magnetic field at the location of the compass swing area, do these steps:
(a) Put a tripod, STD-1167, at the center of the compass swing area.
(b) Remove the magnet assembly from the SCC.
(c) Remove the knob assembly from the SCC.
(d) Attach a master magnetic compass to the SCC with two mounting screws.
NOTE: It is possible to use an accurate standby magnetic compass for a master
magnetic compass.
1) Make sure that the N-S and E-W adjustment screws are at neutral.
(e) Put the SCC/master compass assembly on the tripod, STD-1167.
1) Make sure that the assembly is level.
(f) Turn the assembly until the master magnetic compass shows an indication of magnetic
north (N).
(g) Re-install the magnet assembly to the SCC.
(h) Re-install the knob assembly to the SCC.
(i) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of E at the index line.
(j) Make a record of the heading shown on the master magnetic compass.
(k) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of W at the index line.
(l) Make a record of the heading shown on the master magnetic compass.
(m) Turn the magnetic field cancellation adjustment screw on the SCC to decrease the
heading errors in each direction (E and W) to a minimum.
(n) Continue to adjust the SCC dials for each direction (E and W).
1) Use the Magnetic Field Cancellation Adjustment (MFCA) screw until the errors are
at a minimum.
NOTE: Continue to do this procedure until the error in each direction is at a
minimum. When the errors are at a minimum, do not move the MFCA screw
until the compass swing is completed.
(o) Remove the master magnetic compass from the SCC.
34-23-00
F . Four Point Calibration Swing

SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-103
WARNING
PREPARE THE SAFETY-SENSITIVE SYSTEMS FOR THE AIR MODE BEFORE
YOU INSTALL THE DEACTUATORS. IN THE AIR MODE, MANY OF THE
AIRPLANE SYSTEMS CAN OPERATE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(4) Do this task: Prepare to Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-840-801.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-104
(5) Attach an actuator on the Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Proximity Sensor (S1050).

Interlock Valve Proximity Sensor Functional Test, TASK 27-62-61-400-806.
34-23-00
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-105
(6) Attach the deactuators to the face of the air/ground sensors for the nose and main landing
gear, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
NOTE: The installation of the deactuators will energize the landing gear latch solenoid.
Because the landing gear latch solenoid is close to the standby magnetic compass,
the solenoid must be energized to create a normal level of magnetic and electrical
interference during calibration of the compass.
(a) Let the landing gear latch solenoid stay energized for 20 minutes before you continue.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-003
(7) Set the ND mode selector, on the left Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) control panel,
on the glareshield, to the VOR position or to the ILS position.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-017
(8) Lower the mounting bracket for the standby magnetic compass to give sufficient space for the
SCC:
(a) Loosen the screws on the mounting bracket to let it tilt down.
(b) Move the mounting bracket to you and approximately 15 degrees down.
(c) Tighten the screws on the mounting bracket.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-020-001
(9) Remove the lower left and upper right mounting screws on the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-480-001
(10) Use the two mounting screws to install the SCC on the face of the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-020-002
(11) Disconnect the electrical connectors from the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-003
(12) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of E at the index line.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-001
(13) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-004
(14) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of W at the index line.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-002
(15) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-005
(16) Turn the E-W adjustment screw on the standby magnetic compass until the error in the last two
recorded values is at a minimum.
NOTE: Divide the error in each of the two directions as equally as possible.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-006
(17) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of N at the index line.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-003
(18) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-007
(19) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of S at the index line.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-004
(20) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass.
34-23-00
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-008
(21) Turn the N-S adjustment screw on the standby magnetic compass until the error in the last two
recorded values is at a minimum.
NOTE: Divide the error in each of the two directions as equally as possible.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-009
(22) Continue to adjust the SCC dials for each pair of directions (E-W, N-S).
(a) Turn the E-W and N-S adjustment screws until the errors are at a minimum.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-019
(23) Continue to do this procedure until the error in each pair of directions is at a minimum.
(a) Start with E-W and turn the E-W adjustment screw.
(b) Do N-S and turn the N-S adjustment screw.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-010
(24) When the errors are at a minimum, do the steps that follow for the twelve point accuracy swing.
G. Twelve Point Accuracy Swing and Compass Correction Card
SUBTASK 34-23-00-580-003
(1) Move the airplane to a location near the center of the compass swing area.
NOTE: For each of the magnetic headings that follow, the remaining deviation for the standby
magnetic compass must not be more than ±5 degrees.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-011
(2) Adjust the SCC dials to indicate these magnetic headings: 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 210,
240, 270, 300, and 330 degrees.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-005
(3) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, MH, and the standby compass heading, CH, for
each 30 degree increment.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-111
(4) Put the compass correction card, STD-7061, next to the compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-006
(5) Make a record of the standby compass heading, CH, in the steer column of the compass
correction card, STD-7061, for each 30 degree heading increment.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-020
(6) If the remaining deviation measurement is greater than 5 degrees, do one or more of these
steps:
(a) Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass - Degaussing, TASK 34-23-00-820-803.
(b) Confirm there are no magnetic influences near the compass that could be impacting the
measurements such as non-essential ground equipment, non-ferrous material, cell phone
or laptop near the compass.
NOTE: A cell phone can affect compass readings. Cell phones emit electromagnetic
fields, which can interfere with the magnetic field sensed by a compass and
cause it to give incorrect readings.
34-23-00
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-032
(7) If a remaining deviation measurement is greater than the local regulatory accuracy
requirement, replace the Standby Magnetic Compass (TASK 34-23-00-000-801 and
TASK 34-23-00-400-801).
NOTE: Most regulations state the compensated installation may not have a deviation, in level
flight, greater than 10 degrees on any heading.

(b) Remove the SCC.
(c) Install and tighten the mounting screws on the standby magnetic compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-018

(b) Push the mounting bracket up and into the mounting slots.
(c) Tighten the screws on the mounting bracket.

(11) Make sure that the N-S and E-W adjustment screws on the standby compass are at neutral.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-117
(12) Turn the airplane to Magnetic North 000 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading.
(a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle.
(b) The compass rose heading mark.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-007
(13) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)n, and the standby compass heading,
(CH)n.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-008
(14) Calculate and make a record of the north heading deviation, Dn, as follows: Dn = (MH)n -
(CH)n.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-118
(15) Turn the airplane to Magnetic East 090 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading.
(a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle.
(b) The compass rose heading mark.
34-23-00
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-009
(16) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)e, and the standby compass heading,
(CH)e.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-010
(17) Calculate and make a record of the east heading deviation, De, as follows: De = (MH)e -
(CH)e.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-119
(18) Turn the airplane to Magnetic South 180 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading.
(a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle.
(b) The compass rose heading mark.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-011
(19) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)s, and the standby compass heading,
(CH)s.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-012
(20) Calculate and make a record of the south heading deviation, Ds, as follows: Ds = (MH)s -
(CH)s.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-013
(21) Calculate and make a record of the north-south single-cycle error coefficient, C, and its sign as
follows: C = 0.5(Dn - Ds).
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-013
(22) Turn the N-S adjustment screw on the standby compass (while at the south magnetic heading)
to give a compass heading indication of (CH)s - C.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-120
(23) Turn the airplane to Magnetic West 270 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading.
(a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle.
(b) The compass rose heading mark.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-014
(24) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)w, and the standby compass heading,
(CH)w.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-015
(25) Calculate and make a record of the west heading deviation, Dw, as follows: Dw = (MH)w -
(CH)w.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-016
(26) Calculate and make a record of the east-west single-cycle error coefficient, B, and its sign as
follows: B = 0.5(De - Dw).
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-014
(27) Turn the E-W adjustment screw on the standby compass (while at the west magnetic heading)
to give a compass heading indication of (CH)w - B.
F . Twelve Point Correction Swing Procedure
SUBTASK 34-23-00-580-009
(1) Move the airplane to a location near the center of the compass swing area.
NOTE: For each of the magnetic headings that follow, the remaining deviation for the standby
magnetic compass must not be more than ±5 degrees.
34-23-00
SUBTASK 34-23-00-580-010
(2) Turn the airplane to within +/-0.2 degree of 000, 030, 060, 090, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240, 270,
300 and 330 degrees using (a) or (b) for each target magnetic heading.
(a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle.
(b) The compass rose heading mark.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-017
(3) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, MH, and standby compass heading, CH, for
each 30 degree increment.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-018
(4) Calculate the deviation, D, for each 30 degree heading as follows: D = MH - CH.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-020
(5) Record the deviation, D, for each 30 degree magnetic heading onto the steer column of the
compass correction card, STD-7061.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-121
(6) Put the compass correction card, STD-7061, next to the compass.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-021
(7) If the remaining deviation measurement is greater than 5 degrees, do one or more of these
steps:
(a) Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass - Degaussing, TASK 34-23-00-820-803.
(b) Confirm there are no magnetic influences near the compass that could be impacting the
measurements such as non-essential ground equipment, non-ferrous material, cell phone
or laptop near the compass.
NOTE: A cell phone can affect compass readings. Cell phones emit electromagnetic
fields, which can interfere with the magnetic field sensed by a compass and
cause it to give incorrect readings.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-031
(8) If a remaining deviation measurement is greater than the local regulatory accuracy
requirement, replace the Standby Magnetic Compass (TASK 34-23-00-000-801 and
TASK 34-23-00-400-801).
NOTE: Most regulations state the compensated installation may not have a deviation, in level
flight, greater than 10 degrees on any heading.

7. Standby Magnetic Compass - Degaussing
(Figure 203)
A. General
(1) Use tools that are not magnetic to adjust the standby magnetic compass.
B. Tools/Equipment
Reference Description
STD-4745 Compass - Handheld
STD-6158 Coil - Demagnetizing, AC
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
D. Prepare for Standby Magnetic Compass Degaussing
SUBTASK 34-23-00-840-003
(1) Precautions necessary to demagnetize the standby compass are as follows:
(a) Do not permit the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 to remain within 10 ft (3.05 m) of any
part of aircraft unless it is energized.
(b) Do not operate the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 in vicinity of magnetic compass.
(c) Care should be taken to ensure that the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 is not actually
in contact with surface when used. (To be effective, it should be used as close to surface
as possible.)
E. Standby Magnetic Compass Degaussing Procedure.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-017
(1) Find and identify the area to be demagnetized as follows:
(a) Move a Handheld Compass, STD-4745, into the area adjacent to the standby compass.
1) Make sure that the needle of the Handheld Compass, STD-4745, points to magnetic
north before using it.
(b) If the Handheld Compass, STD-4745, needle moves away from magnetic north, identify
the area for demagnetization.
(2) Demagnetize the standby compass area to restore to normal configuration (area about
windshields and flight compartment) as follows: (Figure 203)
(a) Deactivate the standby magnetic compass. Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass -
Deactivation, TASK 34-23-00-040-801.
(b) Remove the standby compass and store it in an area away from the aircraft.
(c) Energize the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 at a distance of at least 10 ft (3.05 m)
from the aircraft.
34-23-00
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU OBEY THE PROCEDURES TO REMOVE THE
MAGNETIC PARTICLES FROM THE WINDSHIELD AND THE FLIGHT
COMPARTMENT AREAS. KEEP THE TOOL ABOVE THE LOWER PART
OF THE WINDSHIELD SILLS. THIS WILL PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE
INSTRUMENTS.
(d) Move the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 slowly towards windshield areas, bring the
AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 as close as possible to the structure without touching
the structure. Move it in series of parallel strokes over the entire windshield area.
NOTE: The windshield area is defined as the area from top of windshield aft for a
distance of 36 in. (914.4 mm), bounded on each side by the left and right sliding
windshields.
(e) Demagnetize the windshield screws by moving the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 in
line with the screws.
(f) Slowly withdraw the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 at least 10 ft (3.05 m) from the
aircraft before deenergizing.
(g) Check the areas that are degaussed with a Handheld Compass, STD-4745 for signs of
any remaining magnetization. If magnetization still exists, repeat process of degaussing
until evidence of magnetization disappears.
(h) When the area is satisfactorily demagnetized, install the standby compass.
(i) Activate the standby magnetic compass. Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass -
Activation, TASK 34-23-00-440-801.
SUBTASK 34-23-00-700-002
(3) Do a check of the standby magnetic compass system. Do this task: Standby Magnetic
Compass - Compass Rose or Inertial Reference System (IRS) Method,
TASK 34-23-00-820-802 or Standby Magnetic Compass Swing - Standby Compass Calibrator
(SCC) Method, TASK 34-23-00-820-801.

343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH AMETEK NON-MOD A COMPASS C-5L
2) Wind 1 inch wide Scotch No. 24 wire mesh tape around the junction of the electrical
connector [3] and standby magnetic compass [1] a minimum of three times.
NOTE: Securing the connector with tape only applies to AMETEK C-5L compass
that has not been modified to MOD A. An “A” as a suffix to the serial
number indicate a MOD A configuration.
NOTE: The tape must touch against the rear of the standby magnetic compass
case. Keep sufficient tension on the tape while you wind the junction to
make it the shape of the connector. You can use thinner tape, if you wind
the connector with a minimum overlap of 50 percent. Wind all parts of the
connector within 1 inch of the compass with a minimum of three wrappings.
T emporarily secure the end of the tape.
3) Wind the mesh tape a minimum of two times with 1 inch wide Scotch No. 70 or
A-A-59163 Type I self-fusing silicone rubber tape.
NOTE: Keep sufficient tension on the tape while you wind the junction to make it
the shape of the connector You can use thinner tape, if you wind the
connector with a minimum overlap of 50 percent. Wind all of the wire mesh
tape with a minimum of two wrappings of the silicone rubber tape.
4) If the connector is removed for any reason, discard all tape and repeat step (d)
above using new tape.
RYR ALL
(e) Install the screws [2] at the corners of the standby magnetic compass [1].

2. Standby Attitude Reference System - System Test
A. References
Reference Title
24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201)
24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197; AIRPLANES WITHOUT THE ALTERNATE NAVIGATION SYSTEM
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-001
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-003
(2) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-004
(3) Let the gyro get to full speed.
NOTE: The gyro will reach full speed approximately 3 minutes after you supply power.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-006
(4) Pull and release the cage knob on the standby indicator.
NOTE: Do not let the knob hit against the front of the indicator.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-750-001
(5) After five minutes, make sure that the attitude data on the Standby Attitude Indicator is the
same as the captain’s attitude display ± 2 degrees.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-007
(6) Open this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
D 9 C01387 STBY ATT IND
SUBTASK 34-24-00-750-002
(7) Make sure the GYRO flag comes into view in less than one second.
34-24-00
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197; AIRPLANES WITHOUT THE ALTERNATE NAVIGATION SYSTEM
(Continued)
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-008
(8) Close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
D 9 C01387 STBY ATT IND
SUBTASK 34-24-00-750-004
(9) Make sure the GYRO flag goes out of view within 3 minutes.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-009
(10) Tune the captain's VHF NAV receiver to the frequency of 108.35 MHz.
NOTE: To set the frequency, turn the frequency selector until the selected frequency shows in
the STANDBY display window. Then, push the TFR switch. The frequency will show in
the ACTIVE display window. The frequency of 108.35 MHz is the test frequency for the
ILS.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-010
(11) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the APP position.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-740-001
(12) Push the TEST switch on the captain's VHF NAV control panel.
(a) Make sure that the G/S and LOC flags come into view and then go out of view in less
than five seconds.
(b) Make sure the localizer deviation bar moves one mark left and the glide slope deviation
bar moves one mark up.
(c) Make sure the localizer deviation bar moves one mark right and the glide slope deviation
bar moves one mark down.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-011
(13) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the B/CRS position.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-740-003
(14) Push the TEST switch on the captain's VHF NAV control panel.
(a) Make sure the LOC flag comes into view and then goes out of view in less than five
seconds.
(b) Make sure the glide slope deviation bar and the G/S flag are out of view.
(c) Make sure the localizer deviation bar moves to the right side of the center and then to the
left side of the center.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-012
(15) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the OFF position.
SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-013
(16) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

E. Operational Test of the Dedicated Battery System and Battery Pack for the Integrated
Standby Flight Display
SUBTASK 34-24-02-210-006
(1) Do a check to see if the ISFD dedicated battery system (E4-1) and battery pack are
serviceable:
34-24-02
(a) Make sure that the red FAULT light on the front of the battery charger is not on.
NOTE: The red FAULT light shows that the battery charger or the battery pack are not
serviceable. The battery charger or battery pack can be not serviceable because
of problems with battery charger operating temperature, battery charger voltage
output, or battery pack cell voltage.
NOTE: If the red FAULT light is not on and a display shows on the integrated standby
flight display, the battery charger and battery are serviceable.
(b) Open circuit breaker on the front of the ISFD dedicated battery charger.
(c) Close circuit breaker on the front of the ISFD dedicated battery charger.
(d) Make sure that the yellow “ALT”, “SPD”, “ATT”, and “INIT XXs” flags are displayed on the
ISFD for approximately 10 to 15 seconds after power up.
NOTE: “XXs” refers to the time remaining (in seconds) for the ISFD to complete its
initialization. Timer starts at 90s and counts down to 0s.
(e) After 15 seconds, make sure that the display still show “ATT” and “INIT XXs” on the ISFD.
(f) After 120 seconds, make sure that the display change to an attitude display.
(g) Make sure that the BAT SW is in the ON position.
(h) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
D 8 C01551 ISFD
(i) Make sure that the ISFD display is not blank and continues to operate for 5-10 minutes.
NOTE: A fully charged ISFD battery can operate for up to 150 minutes.
(j) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
D 8 C01551 ISFD
F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

(1) If the electrical power is not necessary, turn the power supply off (TASK 24-22-00-860-812).

SUBTASK 34-24-03-710-002
(6) Make sure that the red FAULT light on the face of the battery charger is not on.
NOTE: If the fault light is not on and a display shows on the integrated standby flight display,
the battery charger is serviceable.
(a) The red FAULT light comes on when there is a fault with the battery charger or the
battery, from one or more of these conditions:
1) Battery charger operating temperature is more than the maximum 180°F (82°C) or
less than the minimum 5°F (-15°C).
2) Battery charger circuits do not provide the correct output voltage.
3) Voltage levels of the cells in the battery pack are not equal.

2. Instrument Landing System - Operational Test
A. References
Reference Title
34-21-00-820-801 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC
CDU (P/B 201)
34-21-00-820-802 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU
(P/B 201)
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
C. Prepare for the Test
SUBTASK 34-31-00-710-001
(1) Do these steps to prepare for the operational test:
(a) Set the VHF NAV switch on the instrument switching module to the NORMAL position.
(b) Set the SOURCE switch on the instrument switching module to the AUTO position.
(c) Set the mode selector on the captain's and the first officer's Electronic Flight Instrument
System (EFIS) control panel to the APP position.
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,
132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197; AIRPLANES WITH THE STANDBY ATTITUDE
INDICATOR
(d) Set the Approach Mode Selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the APP
position.
NOTE: The switch can also be labeled Instrument Landing System (ILS).
RYR 198-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341,
343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH INTEGRATED STANDBY FLIGHT DISPLAY (ISFD)
(e) Push the Approach Mode Selector (APP) button on the Integrated Standby Flight Display
(ISFD) until APP is displayed on the ISFD screen.
RYR ALL
(f) Make sure that the Air Data Inertial Reference Unit (ADIRU) is aligned and in the NAV
mode. To align it, do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the
ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from
the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801.
34-31-00
RYR 497-999
(g) Make sure that the ILS, GPS Landing System (GLS) and Global Positioning System
(GPS) lights are not on, on the P5 aft panel.
RYR ALL
(h) Set the captain's and the first officer's course select controls on the Mode Control Panel
(MCP) to the same course as the airplane heading.

(2) Open the nose radome to get access to the localizer antenna [1] (TASK 53-52-00-010-802).
SUBTASK 34-31-31-100-001
(3) Clean the mating surfaces of the localizer antenna [1] and airplane structure
(TASK 20-10-34-110-802).
(a) Apply solvent, B00083, to the mating surfaces of the localizer antenna [1] and airplane
structure with cotton wiper, G00034.
(b) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, and clean the mating surfaces again.
(c) Do these two steps until the mating surfaces are bright, clean, and dry.
34-31-31
SUBTASK 34-31-31-620-001
(4) If the airplane surface has corrosion or other damage, do these steps to prepare the airplane
mating surface:
(a) Apply chemical conversion coating to the airplane mating surface
(TASK 51-21-41-370-802).

(c) Allow primer, C00259, to dry before the screws [2] are installed.
SUBTASK 34-31-31-420-001
(5) Install the localizer antenna [1] as follows:
(a) Remove the protective covers from the electrical connectors [3].
(b) Apply sealant, A00247, to the threads of the screws [2].
(c) Connect the electrical connectors [3] to the localizer antenna [1].
(d) Align the localizer antenna [1] to the screw holes that hold the localizer antenna [1] to the
airplane structure.
(e) Install the screws [2] that attach the localizer antenna [1] to the airplane structure.
(f) Tighten the screws [2] to 80 ±8 in-lb (9.0 ±0.9 N·m).
SUBTASK 34-31-31-760-001
(6) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the localizer antenna [1] and airplane
structure (SWPM 20-20-00).
(a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
(b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohms (1 milliohms) or less.
SUBTASK 34-31-31-420-002
(7) Apply sealant, A00247, around the bases of the localizer antenna [1] to make a corrosion fillet
seal (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).
(a) Apply sealant, A00247, all around the edge of the localizer antenna [1].
(b) Use a sufficient quantity of sealant, A00247, to make the surface smooth.
(c) Remove all the unwanted sealant, A00247, from the area around the antenna.
(d) Let sealant, A00247, dry for the correct cure time.
SUBTASK 34-31-31-410-001
(8) Close the nose radome (TASK 53-52-00-410-802).

2. Part Number Check of the Software
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions to check the part number (PN) of the software In MMR 1 and
MMR 2 using headphones/speakers in the flight deck.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
C. Prepare for the checking of the Software PN
SUBTASK 34-31-42-860-016
(1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 34-31-42-700-003
(1) Do these steps to check the software PN:
(a) Push, the NAV 1 knob (for MMR 1) or NAV2 knob (for MMR 2) on the captain’s or first
officer (FO)’s Audio Control Panel to listen to MMR 1 or MMR 2.
34-31-42
1) Rotate, the NAV 1 knob (for MMR 1) or NAV2 knob (for MMR 2) on the captain’s or
FO’s Audio Control Panel as necessary to adjust the volume to a desired level.
(b) Set a ILS frequency of 108.10 MHz on the captain's or first officer's navigation control
panel (NCP) by following one of these options:
NOTE: The option is dependant on the airplane configuration.
1) Option 1:
a) Push the MODE key (V or reverse V) until “ILS” is displayed in the STBY
(lower) window of the NCP .
b) Push the number “108.10” using the NCP keypad.
c) Push the ACT/STBY transfer key until “ILS 108.10” is displayed in the ACT
(upper) window on the NCP .
2) Option 2:
a) Rotate the outer and inner knobs to dial the ILS frequency “108.10” in the right
(STANDBY) window.
b) Push the TFR key to move the frequency from the right (STANDBY) to the left
(ACTIVE) window.
3) Push, the TEST button on the captain’s NCP to initiate a self-test of MMR 1 or on
the FO’s NCP to initiate a self-test of MMR 2
4) Record, the installed software PN readout during the MMR 1 or MMR 2 self-test:
• “MMR SYSTEM PART NUMBER XXXXXXXX-XXXX” (Not Required)
• “SOFTWARE PART NUMBER XXXXX-XXXX-XXXX” (34 MMR OPS)
• “CONFIGURATION PART NUMBER XXXXX-XXXX-XXXX” (34 MMR OSS)
NOTE: Push the TEST button again, as necessary until all installed software PNs
have been recorded.
(c) If the software PNs are correct, then software installation is not needed.
(d) If the software PNs are not correct, then install the software.
34-31-42-470-801Software Installation with a PDLPDF p. 528

3. Software Installation with a PDL
A. General
(1) This procedure gives instructions to install the Operational Program Software (OPS) and the
operational configuration software (OSS) into the Multi-Mode Receiver (MMR) with a Portable
Data Loader (PDL). Load the OPS software first, then load the OSS software.
NOTE: The PDL must be connected to the MMR receiver through the RJ45 connector on the
front of the receiver. When connected directly to the MMR front connector, an Ethernet
cable is required.
(2) A PDL is not a Boeing supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier manual for instructions for
operation. Some PDL have a disk drive for software installation from disks. If the PDL has an
internal mass storage device, then disks are not necessary.
34-31-42
(3) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer
are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as
preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders
procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current
capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.
(4) For general information for software installation times and data loaders, do this task:
On-Airplane Software - Installation, TASK 20-15-11-400-801.
B. Special Tools and Equipment
(1) Portable Data Loader:
(2) Ethernet cable.
(3) MMR OPSand MMR OSS software.

F . MMR NVM Download
SUBTASK 34-31-42-970-001
(1) Download the MMR NVM data as follows:
CAUTION
DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS, OR OTHER CONDUCTORS.
IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE
CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS.
(a) Remove the maintenance port access cover from the MMR.
(b) Put the USB drive into the USB port on the MMR.
(c) Remove the safety tag and close the applicable circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2
(d) Make sure that the top three lights flash yellow in a sequence from top to bottom.
NOTE: This flash pattern shows that the NVM download is in progress. The pattern will
change while the download continues but the lights will stay yellow.
(e) Make sure that the top three lights flash green in the sequence that follows:
NOTE: This flash pattern shows that the NVM download completed. This flash pattern
will repeat with no end. It is safe to turn off the MMR and to remove the USB
drive at this time.
1) In sequence from top to bottom.
2) All three lights at the same time.

SUBTASK 34-32-00-710-002
(1) Do this task: Marker Beacon System - Operational Test, TASK 34-32-00-710-801.
E. Marker Beacon System Test
SUBTASK 34-32-00-860-007
(1) Push the receiver volume controls for marker beacon, MKR, on each audio selector panel to
set the volume to off.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-480-001
(2) Put the NAV/COMM ramp test set, COM-1913 or the equivalent test set, directly below the
marker beacon antenna.
(a) Put the test set on a non-metal surface.
(b) Make sure that the test set antenna is 36 ±2 in. (91 ±5 cm) below the marker beacon
antenna.
(c) Make sure that the test set faces the nose landing gear.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-730-001
(3) Set the NAV/COMM ramp test set, COM-1913, to supply a marker beacon signal of 75 MHz
with a 400 Hz modulation.
NOTE: If the antenna on the test set is not a marker beacon test antenna tuned at 75 MHz, it
is not easy to get the test results.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-700-001
(4) Make sure that power setting indication starts at -19 dBm minimum and adjusts by 1 dBm
increments to a maximum of -15 dBm.
(5) Make sure that the outer marker indication, OM, shows on the captain's and the first officer's
EFIS displays.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-860-008
(6) Push the receiver volume control for marker beacon, MKR, on the captain's audio control panel
to set the volume to on.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-730-002
(7) Turn the receiver volume control clockwise for marker beacon, MKR, on the captain's audio
control panel.
(a) Make sure that you can hear a tone through the interphone system.
(b) Make sure that you can hear a tone at the captain's audio selector panel with a headset.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-860-009
(8) Push the receiver volume control for marker beacon, MKR, on the captain's audio selector
panel to set the volume to off.

panel to set the volume to on.

headset.
SUBTASK 34-32-00-860-011

SUBTASK 34-32-00-730-005

officer's EFIS displays.

3. Marker Beacon Antenna with Gasket - Removal
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This procedure is used for the removal of antennas that use Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per
737–SL-20–045.
NOTE: Reference the Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog for the gasket part number.
(2) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do the steps that
follow:
(a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each a D check.
(b) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion on the antenna and gasket after their
removal.
(c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the antenna gasket.
1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
100 Lower Half of Fuselage

SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-006
(1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 1 C01374 RADIO NAVIGATION VOR/MKR BCN 1
SUBTASK 34-32-11-020-002
(2) Remove the marker beacon antenna [1]:
(a) Remove the six bolts [2] from the antenna base.
CAUTION
MOVE THE ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS NECESSARY TO DISCONNECT
CABLES. DAMAGE TO ANTENNA CABLES CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL
CABLES.
(b) Lower the marker beacon antenna [1] until you can get access to the coaxial connector
[3].
(c) Disconnect the coaxial connector [3] from the marker beacon antenna [1].
(d) Remove the marker beacon antenna [1].
(e) Remove and discard the gasket [4].
NOTE: For the Aerobond gasket, special attention must be used to remove the gel
material residue to prevent silicone oil contamination on other parts of the
airplane skin, which may cause paint adhesion difficulties.

F . Marker Beacon Antenna Installation
SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-002
(1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 1 C01374 RADIO NAVIGATION VOR/MKR BCN 1
SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-001
(2) Clean the airplane mating surface.
WARNING
DO NOT GET THE SOLVENT IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE IN THE FUMES FROM THE SOLVENT . PUT ON
PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THE
SOLVENT . KEEP THE SOLVENT AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND
HEAT . THE SOLVENT IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE, WHICH CAN
CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(a) Clean the airplane mating surface with cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 88
solvent, B01008 (TASK 20-30-88-910-801).
(b) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, and clean the airplane mating surface again.
(c) Do these two steps above until the airplane mating surface is clean and dry.
SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-002
(3) If the airplane surface has corrosion or other damage, do these steps to prepare the airplane
mating surface:
(a) Remove the corrosion from the airplane mating surface, do this task: Removal and
Control of Corrosion for Plated or Phosphated Surfaces, TASK 51-21-31-350-806.
34-32-11
(b) To apply a layer of coating, C00064, to the airplane mating surface, do this task:
Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM 1200 Aero, or Bonderite M-CR
1200S Aero Application Process, TASK 51-21-41-370-802.
SUBTASK 34-32-11-420-001
(4) Install the marker beacon antenna [1].
(a) Connect the coaxial connector [3] to the marker beacon antenna [1].
(b) Put the marker beacon antenna [1] in the correct position on the airplane surface.
(c) Install five of the six bolts [2] in the base of the marker beacon antenna [1].
(d) Manually tighten the bolts [2] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
(e) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the baseplate of the marker beacon
antenna [1] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00).
NOTE: Use the empty bolt hole to get access to the antenna baseplate.
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohms) or
less.
(f) Install the last bolt [2].
1) Manually tighten the bolt [2] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 34-32-11-390-001
(5) Apply aerodynamic sealant.
(a) Apply an aerodynamic fillet seal around the base of the marker beacon antenna [1] with
sealant, A00247 (TASK 51-31-00-390-806 and TASK 20-30-11-910-801).
NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation
until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The
deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks
(SL 20-043).
(b) Use the hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810, to make a smooth
45-degree fillet.
(c) Apply sealant, A00247, to the heads of the bolts [2] (TASK 51-31-00-390-806 and
TASK 20-30-11-910-801).
NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation
until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The
deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks
(SL 20-043).
(d) Let the sealant dry for the correct cure time.
SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-003
(6) Close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name

G. Marker Beacon Antenna Installation Test
SUBTASK 34-32-11-730-001
(1) Test the marker beacon antenna [1], do these steps:
(a) Make sure that the MKR controls on all the audio selector panels are off.
34-32-11
(b) Put the NAV/COMM ramp test set, COM-1913, or equivalent test set directly below the
marker beacon antenna.
1) Put the test set on a non-metal surface.
2) Make sure that the test set antenna is 36 ±2 in. (91 ±5 cm) below the marker
beacon antenna.
3) Make sure that the test set faces to the nose landing gear.
(c) Set the NAV/COMM ramp test set, COM-1913, or equivalent test set to supply a marker
beacon signal of 75 MHz with a 400 Hz modulation.
NOTE: If the antenna on the test set is not a marker beacon test antenna tuned at 75
MHz, it is not easy to get the test results.
(d) Make sure that power setting indication starts at -19 dBm minimum and increments by 1
dBm to a maximum of -15 dBm.
(e) Make sure that the OUTER (blue) marker beacon indication of “OM” on the captain's and
first officer's Primary Flight Display (PFD) comes into view.
H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 34-32-11-080-001
(1) Remove the NAV/COMM ramp test set, COM-1913, or equivalent test set.

5. Marker Beacon Antenna with Gasket - Installation
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This procedure is used for the installation of antennas with Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per
737–SL-20–045.
(2) As a full certification of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do the steps that follow:
(a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check.
(b) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the antenna and gasket after their removal.
(c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the antenna gasket.
1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-007
(1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 1 C01374 RADIO NAVIGATION VOR/MKR BCN 1
SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-003
(2) Clean the airplane mating surface:
WARNING
DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS
ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE.
OBEY THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) FOR SOLVENTS.
OBEY LOCAL REGULATIONS FOR THE CORRECT PROCEDURES TO
USE OR DISCARD SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
(a) Clean the airplane mating surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 88
solvent, B01008 (TASK 20-30-88-910-801).
(b) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, and clean the airplane mating surface again.
(c) Do these two steps above until the airplane mating surface is clean and dry.
SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-004
(3) If the airplane surface has corrosion or other damage, do these steps to prepare the airplane
mating surface:
(a) Do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Plated or Phosphated Surfaces,
TASK 51-21-31-350-806
(b) To apply a layer of coating, C00064, to the airplane mating surface, do this task:
Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM 1200 Aero, or Bonderite M-CR
1200S Aero Application Process, TASK 51-21-41-370-802.
SUBTASK 34-32-11-420-002
(4) Install the marker beacon antenna [1]:
(a) Remove the protective film from each side of the gasket [4].
NOTE: Reference the Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog for the gasket part number.
(b) Put the gasket [4] on the marker beacon antenna.
(c) Connect the coaxial connector [3] to the marker beacon antenna [1].
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY SEALANT TO THE EDGES OF THE ANTENNA. THE
GASKET RELEASES THE MOISTURE. IF YOU SEAL THE EDGES, THE
MOISTURE WILL STAY . THIS CAN CAUSE CORROSION DAMAGE TO
THE AIRPLANE, AND ANTENNA MATING SURFACES.
(d) Put the marker beacon antenna [1] in the correct position on the airplane surface.
(e) Install five of the six bolts [2] in the base of the marker beacon antenna [1].
34-32-11
1) Manually tighten the bolts [2] to 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m).
NOTE: Since the gel material of the gasket is compressible, the bolts must be
re-torqued 15 minutes after the installation to ensure tightness.
2) After 15 minutes, manually torque the bolts [2] to 16.5 ±1.5 in-lb (1.86 ±0.17 N·m).
NOTE: To help prevent cracks, each antenna fastener could be tightened to a few
pound-inches at a time until all fasteners are tightened. After a few minutes,
each fastener can be tightened a few more pound-inches. This is repeated
until each fastener is tightened to the recommended torque value.
(f) Measure the resistance between the baseplate of the marker beacon antenna [1] and the
airplane skin with an ohmmeter, STD-1045, or a intrinsically safe approved bonding
meter, COM-1550
NOTE: Use the empty bolt hole to get access to the antenna baseplate.
1) Make sure that the resistance is less than 2.5 milliohms.
(g) Install the last bolt [2].
NOTE: Since the gel material of the gasket is compressible, the bolt must be re-torqued
15 minutes of the installation to ensure tightness.
SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-008
(5) Close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1

2. Low Range Radio Altimeter System - Deactivation
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) This procedure removes electrical power to the LRRA System.
NOTE: There are four LRRA antennas installed on the bottom of the airplane. The No. 1
(M1737) and No. 2 (M1738) transmit antennas are the outer antennas. The No. 1
(M1739) and the No. 2 (M1740) receive antennas are the inner antennas.
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left
118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right
123 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left
124 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right
211 Flight Compartment - Left
212 Flight Compartment - Right
C. Procedure
NOTE: For airplanes with predictive wind shear weather radar systems, open the weather radar
(WXR) transceiver circuit breaker to make sure that the WXR system does not come on.
The radio altimeter supplies radio altitude data to the WXR transceiver. The WXR
transceiver uses the radio altitude data to turn the WXR system on and off.

(5) Install the Aeroflex ALT-8000 test set (radio altimeter test set, COM-14227).
NOTE: Refer to the ALT-8000 Radio Altimeter Test Set operation manual for detailed
information.
(a) Place the test set no more than 10 ft (3.0 m) from the radio altimeter antennas.
(b) Connect the 20 ft (6.1 m) Low Loss Radio Frequency (RF) Coax Cables to the color
coded test set TX/RX Threaded Neill-Concelman (TNC) connectors.
(c) Push the power ON/OFF switch for a minimum of 1 second to power the test set.
(d) The power up screen and load progress bar are shown.
NOTE: The test set user interface is a touch screen control panel. The Launch Bar is a
vertical scrolling menu shown on the left side of the touch screen that provides
access to the function icons.
(e) Touch the light gray bar to open the Launch Bar.
(f) Touch Test Setup to show the Test Setup window.
NOTE: This window is used to configure the test set operational parameters.
(g) Touch the light gray bar to close the Launch Bar.

General tab:
1) Connection Type - Coupler
2) UUT Detect Mode - Auto
3) Level Mode - Auto.

34-33-00

2) RX Cable Loss - See cable for value in dBs
3) TX Coupler Loss - See TX Antenna Coupler for value in dBs
4) RX Coupler Loss - See RX Antenna Coupler for value in dBs.
(j) Touch Delay Calibration to show the Delay Calibration screen.
NOTE: This screen starts the calibration procedure for the test set RF coaxial cable
delay.
1) Connect the ends of the TX and RX cables together with the supplied TNC
connector.
2) Touch Start to start delay calibration.
NOTE: Delay calibration can not be aborted once started. The calibration process
is automatic and the Test Setup screen is shown when calibration is
completed.
3) Disconnect the TNC connector from the TX and RX cables.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-480-004
(6) Do these steps to install the antenna couplers:
NOTE: The Aeroflex ALT-8000 test set (radio altimeter test set, COM-14227) will not function
correctly if the antenna couplers are placed over the wrong aircraft antennas. You do
not see any TX power from the UUT and the test would not work.
(a) Select and assemble the sectional pole lengths to support the antenna couplers.
(b) Mount the antenna coupler to the end of each assembled pole.
(c) Push down on each pole assembly until the gas shock compresses and locks the
retaining clamp.
(d) Raise the TX pole assembly and place the antenna coupler over the applicable radio
altimeter transmit antenna.
1) If the pole is vertical, release the gas shock retaining clamp to apply upward
pressure on the antenna coupler.
(e) Raise the RX pole assembly and place the antenna coupler over the applicable radio
altimeter receive antenna.
1) When the pole is vertical, release the gas shock retaining clamp to apply upward
pressure on the antenna coupler.
(f) Connect the TX and RX coax cables to the TX and RX antenna couplers TNC connector.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-031

H. Radio Altitude Simulation Test (Using the Atlantis DRA707 Test Set)
SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-015
(1) Prepare the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922, for the altitude simulation, do these steps:
(a) Set the power ON/OFF switch to the ON position.
1) Make sure that the 5 VDC and HOLDING lights come on.
(b) Set the NO COMPUTED DATA switches to the NORMAL position.
(c) Push and release the PRES ALT key.
1) Make sure that PRES ALT shows on the Light Emitting Diode (LED)s.
(d) Use the keypad to put in a value of +4000 feet.
(e) Push and release the ENTER key.
1) Make sure that the radio altitude value shown on the EFIS displays is blank.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-016
(2) Prepare the captain's and the first officer's EFIS control panels for the simulation.
(a) Push and release the RST (reset) button.
(b) Turn the DH control to show DH 450 at the captain's EFIS display.
(c) Turn the DH control to show DH 400 at the first officer's EFIS display.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-017
(3) Set these controls on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922:
(a) Push and release the START ALT key.
1) Make sure that START ALT shown on the LEDs.
(b) Use the keypad to put in a value of +4000 feet.
(c) Push and release the ENTER key.
1) Make sure that the LEDs show START ALT +4000.
(d) Push and release the STOP ALT key.
1) Make sure that the LEDs show STOP ALT .
(e) Use the keypad to put in a value of -20 feet.
(f) Push and release the ENTER key.
1) Make sure that the LEDs show STOP ALT -20.
(g) Push and release the VERT SPD key.
1) Make sure that the LEDs show VERT SPD.
(h) Use the keypad to put in a value of -4000 (feet per minute).
(i) Push and release the ENTER key.
1) Make sure that the LEDs show VERT SPD -4000.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-730-009
(4) Do the altitude ramp-down test (typical).
(a) Push the RAMP/HOLD key on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922.
1) Make sure that the RAMPING light comes on.
(b) Look for these indications on the captain's and the first officer's EFIS displays.
1) The radio altitude goes out of view for approximately 22.5 seconds while the altitude
on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922, decreases from 4000 to 2500 feet.
34-33-00
(c) After the time-out of 22.5 seconds (previous step), a radio altitude of 2500 feet comes
into view on the EFIS displays and decreases toward zero.
NOTE: The EFIS displays show the radio altitude set on the radio altimeter test set,
COM-1922, within the limit of 2500 feet to -20 feet.
(d) Look for these indications on the captain's EFIS display when the radio altitude
decreases to 450 feet:
1) The DH value changes to a yellow color and flashes for 3 seconds.
2) The radio altitude continues to decrease toward zero.
(e) Look for these indications on the first officer's EFIS display when the radio altitude
decreases to 400 feet:
1) The DH value changes to a yellow color and flashes for 3 seconds.
2) The DH value flashes for approximately 3 seconds.
3) The radio altitude continues to decrease toward zero.
(f) Look for these indications on the EFIS displays while the radio altitude decreases to zero
feet:
1) The radio altitude value changes to a white color.
2) The DH value changes to the numbers set at the captain's and the first officer's
EFIS control panels.
I. Radio Altitude Simulation Test (Using Aeroflex ALT-8000 Test Set) (Alternate)
SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-032
(1) Prepare the Aeroflex ALT-8000 test set (radio altimeter test set, COM-14227), for the altitude
simulation:
(a) Touch Alt. Ind. Zero to show the Altitude Indicator Zero screen.
NOTE: The test set is now simulating 0 ft (0 m) at the end of the ALT-8000 RF coax
cables.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-033
(2) Prepare the captain's and the first officer's EFIS control panels for the simulation.
(a) Push and release the RST (reset) button.
(b) Turn the DH control to show DH 450 at the captain's EFIS display.
(c) Turn the DH control to show DH 400 at the first officer's EFIS display.
SUBTASK 34-33-00-730-012
(3) Do the altitude ramp-down test:
(a) Touch the light gray bar to open the Launch Bar.
(b) Touch Simulation window to show the Simulation window.
NOTE: The Simulation window is the main test screen and provides visual access to
control parameters and test data.
(c) Touch the light gray bar to close the Launch Bar.
(d) Set these values in the Control area of the Simulation window:
NOTE: When a numeric data field is touched for editing, a data entry pop-up window is
shown. A numeric keypad, data slew bar or rotary knob pop-up window can be
used to enter a value.
1) Start Altitude = 3000 ft (914.4 m)
34-33-00
2) Stop Altitude = 0 ft (0 m)
3) Altitude Rate = 100 ft/min (0.508 m/s).
NOTE: DH trips should be completed with an altitude ramp-down and descent rate
of 100 ft/min or less, to let the DH indicator and any audible warning
operate correctly.
(e) Touch Run to start simulation.
NOTE: Altitude Pause is shown.
NOTE: To pause simulation at any point, touch Altitude Pause. The Current Altitude can
be changed and the simulation is started again with a touch of Altitude Resume.
1) The test set Current Altitude shows 3000 ft (914.4 m) and starts to decrease toward
0 ft (0 m).
(f) Make sure that the captain's and first officers EFIS display show these values:
1) No radio altitude shows until the Current Altitude reaches 2500 ft (762.0 m).
2) When the Current Altitude reaches 450 ft (137.2 m), the decision height indications
on the captain's EFIS display change.
3) When the Current Altitude reaches 400 ft (121.9 m), the decision height indications
on the first officers EFIS display change.
4) The Current Altitude on the test set and the radio altitude on the EFIS display
continue to decrease to 0 ft (0 m).
(g) Touch Stop to end the simulation.

34-33-00-710-801Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - Operational TestPDF p. 601
Open original AMM PDF - page 601 ↗ 
2. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - Operational Test
A. General
(1) The operational test includes a LRRA Interface To Display Electronic Unit test.
(2) The operational test makes sure the interface between the transceiver and the displays is ok.
(3) The operational test does not include a check of the LRRA antennas.
(4) This test will make sure the that the radio altimeter operates correctly after a suspected 5G
interference.
(a) There can be 5G interference to the radio altimeter signals because of the frequency
spectrum (3.4 GHz - 4.2 GHz, 4.4 GHz - 4.9 GHz), antenna type, and power levels used
by the 5G technology. The radio altimeters can become inoperative or can supply
erroneous data, which can affect other systems on the airplane that use radio altimeter
data.
1) Follow your airline policy for reporting the specific event.
2) For more information refer to 737NG-FTD-34-21001.

Open original AMM PDF - page 602 ↗ 
3. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - System Test
A. General
(1) The system test makes sure that the interface between the Air/Ground relays is ok and the
transmit and receive antennas operate correctly.
(2) The system test includes these tests:
(a) The LRRA Air/Ground Discrete Input Test
(b) The LRRA Antenna Coaxial Cable Test.
1) Interface from LRRA equipment rack connector to antenna connector.
2) Interface from LRRA R/T to antenna connector.
(3) For airplanes with predictive wind shear weather radar systems, open the Weather Radar
(WXR) transceiver circuit breaker to make sure that the WXR system does not come on. The
radio altimeter supplies radio altitude data to the WXR transceiver. The WXR transceiver uses
the radio altitude data to turn the WXR system on and off.

3. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with Gasket
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This task includes the steps to remove the Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) antenna.
(2) The LRRA antenna can be removed by one of these two methods:
• Inside the fuselage
• Outside the fuselage.
(a) The application of the self-leveling sealant and connector compound can prevent removal
of the antenna from outside the fuselage.
(3) Imprints on the fuselage skin caused by the gasket wire mesh are permitted. If such imprints
are found, then no maintenance action is necessary.

5. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with Gasket
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This task includes the steps to install the Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) antenna.
(2) The LRRA antenna can be installed by one of these two methods:
• Inside the fuselage
• Outside the fuselage.
(a) The antenna must be installed from inside the fuselage if the self-leveling sealant and
connector compound will be applied. This method makes sure that sufficient access is
allowed for the correct installation of the sealant and compound.
(b) If the self-leveling sealant and connector compound will be deferred, then the antenna
can be installed from outside the fuselage.

H. LRRA Antenna Installation from Inside the Fuselage
NOTE: It is necessary to access the antenna from inside the fuselage to apply the self-leveling
sealant and connector compound.
SUBTASK 34-33-11-400-001
(1) Install the new gasket [5] onto the antenna [1].
(a) Discard the O-ring supplied with the antenna [1].
(b) Remove the protective gasket film from the side of the gasket [5] that will be applied to
the antenna [1].
34-33-11
RYR 349-999; RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131,

(c) Align the holes on the gasket [5] to the holes on the antenna [1].
NOTE: The fasteners may be used to help align the gasket with the antenna.
(d) Push the gasket [5] firmly onto the base plate of the antenna [1].
(e) Remove the protective film from the side of the gasket [5] that will be applied to the
airplane surface.
SUBTASK 34-33-11-400-004
(2) Install the antenna [1].
(a) Put the antenna [1] in the correct position on the airplane surface.
(b) Install the screws [2].
1) Tighten the screws [2] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
2) After 15 minutes, tighten the screws [2] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m).
SUBTASK 34-33-11-700-002
(3) Measure the resistance between the antenna base plate and airplane skin with an intrinsically
safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550 (SWPM 20-20-00).
(a) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm).
SUBTASK 34-33-11-390-005
(4) Apply self-leveling sealant, A50403, or Self-Leveling Green sealant, A50143, or Self-Leveling
Green FR sealant, A50630, around the base of the antenna connector.
NOTE: Operators can defer the application of self-leveling sealant, A50403, or Self-Leveling
Green sealant, A50143, or Self-Leveling Green FR sealant, A50630, to avoid a flight
delay. The deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed 30 days (SL 34-210).
(a) Fill the entire cavity around the antenna connector.
(b) Make sure that the sealant is level or convex and does not extend more than 0.10 in.
(2.54 mm) above the cavity.

D. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Inspection
SUBTASK 34-33-11-200-001
(1) Examine the outer surface of the antenna for a circular area ¼ in. (6.35 mm) or larger that is
not constant and smooth.
(a) If an area is found, replace the antenna, do these tasks:
• Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with O-Ring,
TASK 34-33-11-000-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with
Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-000-803
• Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with O-Ring,
TASK 34-33-11-400-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation
with Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-400-803.
34-33-11
SUBTASK 34-33-11-020-001
(2) Remove the radio altimeter antenna, do this task: Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna
Removal with O-Ring, TASK 34-33-11-000-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna
Removal with Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-000-803.
NOTE: The antenna connector is inspected and cleaned during the connector removal.
SUBTASK 34-33-11-120-001
(3) Remove all unwanted material from around the connector and backplate.
SUBTASK 34-33-11-210-001
(4) This subtask is only for the airplanes with Radio Altimeter antenna P/N DMPN19-1-1 installed:
NOTE: Ignore this Subtask if there is no Radio Altimeter antenna P/N DMPN19-1-1 installed
on the airplane.
(a) Examine the four nuts on the electrical connector for corrosion.
1) If a nut is not there or loose, or has corrosion, replace the antenna
(TASK 34-33-11-000-801 or TASK 34-33-11-000-803 and TASK 34-33-11-400-801
or TASK 34-33-11-400-803).
NOTE: Do not replace nuts that have corrosion. This will change the correct
operation of the antenna.
(b) Examine the antenna connector and backplate for corrosion.
NOTE: If there is corrosion on the surface in the inner diameter of the O-ring seal, but
the connector nuts have no corrosion, do not replace the antenna. It will operate
correctly.
SUBTASK 34-33-11-120-002
(5) Clean the backplate and connector where there is corrosion on the surface.
WARNING
ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS TOXIC AND FLAMMABLE. USE PERSONAL
PROTECTION EQUIPMENT . USE IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA.
(a) Use alcohol, B50073.

(b) Remove excessive alcohol, B50073, by wiping with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034.

INCLUDES HANGARS, TRUCKS, OTHER AIRPLANES. THIS 300 FEET

SUBTASK 34-43-00-860-268
WARNING
DO NOT OPERATE THE WEATHER RADAR WITHIN 3.3 FEET (1 METER) OF
REFUELING OR DE-FUELING OPERATIONS, A FUEL SPILL OR OPEN FUEL
CELLS. OPERATION OF THE WEATHER RADAR WITHIN THE 3.3 FEET (1
METER) LIMIT CAN CAUSE A FIRE OR EXPLOSION. A FIRE OR EXPLOSION
CAN CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE NOSE RADOME IF THE WIND IS MORE THAN 15
KNOTS. IF YOU OPEN THE NOSE RADOME IN A WIND, THE RADOME CAN
MOVE QUICKLY . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
WARNING
DO NOT OPERATE THE WEATHER RADAR WHEN PERSONNEL ARE IN THE
AREA USUALLY ENCLOSED BY THE AIRCRAFT NOSE RADOME OR IN A
HANGAR. THESE CONDITIONS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
NOTE: The hangar restriction DOES NOT apply to the weather radar test mode.

5. Weather Radar Antenna Drive Unit Installation
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This task has the steps to install the weather radar antenna drive unit.
RYR 349-999
(2) An auto alignment process will take place and will require up to 30 minutes to complete
depending on the flight profile.
NOTE: No matter which procedure is done to more quickly auto align the system, the weather
radar system will continue to do its function correctly. But, initially (until auto-alignment
process completes on its own) there could be decreased long range weather detection
(if antenna aims too high) or unwanted ground clutter shown (if antenna aims too low).
(a) Recommended flight profile for auto-alignment:
1) Achieve cruise altitude at minimum 17000 feet above prevailing terrain in radar field
of view.
2) System is in the Auto mode.
NOTE: Switching to the manual mode will interrupt WXR auto-alignment.
3) Un-accelerated straight level flight, no maneuvering.
4) Not over mountainous terrain or large variations of terrain.
NOTE: The automatic alignment feature will work in mountainous terrain. But, it
could take longer to complete.
5) Not in visible weather, no significant weather within the radar field of view between
80 nmi (148 km) and 140 nmi (259 km).
6) Not over water.
NOTE: Flying over water could give weak returns.
RYR ALL

2. Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Inspection
A. General
(1) The purpose of this task is to examine the antenna flat plate for wear to make sure that it is in
a serviceable condition. Types of wear include:
(a) Corrosion
(b) Dents
(c) Holes, gouges and tears
(d) Warping
(e) Foreign objects
(f) Lightning strikes.
RYR 349-999
(2) The antenna flat plate is divided into three zones. This is to help easily identify wear:
(a) Zone 2 is the area outside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center.
(b) Zone 3 is the area inside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center.
(c) Zone 4 is the feed waveguide.
(3) A single radiating waveguide is defined as one of the channels that run parallel between the
two surfaces of the antenna flat plate.
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-348
(4) The antenna flat plate is divided into four zones. This is to help easily identify wear:
(a) Zone 1 is the outer edges outside the waveguide terminal zone or waveguide end plates.
(b) Zone 2 is the area outside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center.
(c) Zone 3 is the area inside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center.
(d) Zone 4 is the feed waveguide.
(5) A single radiating waveguide is defined as one of the channels that run parallel between the
two surfaces of the antenna flat plate.
RYR ALL
(6) If it is necessary to replace the antenna flat plate, refer to Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate
Removal, TASK 34-43-11-000-801 and Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Installation,
TASK 34-43-11-400-801.

H. Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Inspection
(Figure 602)
NOTE: Dents are defined as damage that could have occurred because of the surface being hit by
a blow or crushed by a point load.
NOTE: The manufacturing procedure can cause an antenna flat plate that shows a small quantity of
generalized warping or slow changes in the flat of the surface. The general warping/change
must not be regarded as a dent if it occurs on an area of 2.5 ±0.5 in. (63.5 ±12.7 mm).
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-010
WARNING
YOU MUST WEAR GOGGLES OR A FACE SHIELD WHEN YOU USE THE
EXTERNAL ABRASIVE BLASTING EQUIPMENT . IF YOU DO NOT USE THE
PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT , INJURIES CAN OCCUR.
(1) Examine the antenna flat plate, the flat plate slots, waveguide and interior for corrosion:
(a) If corrosion is found in the slots, then the antenna flat plate must be replaced.
(b) If corrosion is found, remove as follows:
1) Blow off loose material from the two sides of the antenna flat plate with an air
supply, STD-6852.
2) Remove loose material on the two sides of the antenna flat plate with an emery
cloth, STD-6449.
3) Clean the front and rear of the antenna flat plate with alcohol, B00130.
4) Apply coating, C50395 to exposed or bare metal areas on the front or rear surfaces.
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-026
(2) Examine the antenna flat plate for etching, nicks, pits or scratches (front and rear):
(a) An antenna flat plate is unservicable if the etching, nicks, pits, or scratches on the front
surface:
1) Are not caused by the manufacturing process (i.e., brazing, cleaning, honing, tool
no larger than 0.030 in. (0.8 mm), etc.) or not the reasonable consequence of valid
handling procedures and are not collectively limited to less than 25% of the surface
area.
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-011
(3) Examine the antenna flat plate for dents in zone 2 (front and rear):
(a) Dents must be 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) or less in depth.
(b) A maximum of two dents on a single radiating waveguide.
(c) A maximum of seven dents in zone 2 in total.
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-012
(4) Examine the antenna flat plate for dents in zone 3 (front and rear):
(a) Dents must be 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) or less in depth.
(b) A maximum of one dent on a single radiating waveguide.
(c) A maximum of three dents in zone 3 in total.
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-014
(5) Examine the antenna flat plate for dents in zone 4 (front and rear):
(a) No dents are permitted in the feed waveguide (zone 4).
34-43-11
RYR 349-999 (Continued)
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-015
(6) Examine the antenna flat plate (front and rear):
(a) No damage is permitted to the partitions or end plates related to a single radiating
waveguide in which a surface dent has also occurred.
(b) If the front or rear surfaces show through the surface holes (other than slots), or have
breaks or cracks, the unit must be replaced.
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-017
(7) Examine the slots on the front and rear of the antenna flat plate:
(a) Dents that cause damage to the surface slots will make the antenna flat plate
unserviceable.
(b) The surface slot must not show localized dents or signs of mechanical rework, such as
file marks or rough edges.
SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-018
(8) Examine the antenna flat plate outer edge (the outer 1 in. (25 mm), front and rear) for small
dents, bending, marks and handling damage:
(a) These are permitted if they agree with the following criteria:
NOTE: If the anomalies do not agree with the criteria below then the antenna flat plate is
unserviceable.
1) Does not structurally impair the antenna.
2) Does not exceed more than 25% of the circumference of either the front or rear
surface.
3) Does not occur in large numbers on a new production antenna such that the
antenna appears not to be new.
