6. ATC System Test (With the TR-220 Test Set)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
WARNING
USE AN ANTENNA COUPLER WITH THE RAMP TESTER TO SIMULATE AN
AIR MODE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THE AIRPLANE WILL TRANSMIT
ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIRCRAFT IN
THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE
TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
AIRCRAFT .
(1) This system test is a full check of the Air Traffic Control (ATC) system. The system test first
does the ATC - Operational Test and then uses the test set to examine the left and right ATC
systems.
(2) The TR-220 ramp test set, COM-10728, is capable of testing Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon
System (ATCRBS) Mode A, Mode C and Mode S transponders. The operator can select
between an Automatic series of tests and a Manual series of tests. The Test Set will determine
the correct set of tests, either Mode A/C or Mode S upon receiving the transponder Radio
Frequency (RF) signal. The TR-220 ramp test set, COM-10728 can also test Mode S
Transponders with EHS (Enhanced Surveillance) capabilities.
(a) The test set can do all of the tests automatically except the IDENT BUTTON CHECK. You
must do this test manually with the test set.
(b) If a test has failed, the automatic test sequence will stop and a failed message will show.
At the end of the automatic test all data will show.
(c) Completion of these tests satisfy the 24 month ATC transponder maintenance check
requirements.
(3) The TR-220 ramp test set, COM-10728, with software version 5.60 or higher can also test the
Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B) functions for DO-260, DO-260A, and
DO-260B compliant transponders. These tests satisfy the ADS-B Out 24 month ATC
transponder maintenance check requirements.
(4) To do the test manually, set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position to do
each test individually. The test results will show after each test is done. After each test is
completed, you must toggle the MANUAL switch to advance to the next test in the series.
(5) Operation with the UC-584 universal transponder antenna coupler, COM-18775, (preferred) or
coupler TAP-200 used with the test set, reduces RF emissions from the transponder being
tested.
(6) If it is necessary to simulate the aircraft at altitude, notify the local ATC that the transponder
testing is in progress.
34-53-00
(7) Depending on the tool being used, only one T ask Card needs to be completed for each
schedule per the airplane.

(10) Prepare the TR-220 ramp test set, COM-10728 and the antenna coupler for the ATC system
test:
NOTE: The TR-220 ramp test set, COM-10728 has an ‘‘auto test’’ function which checks more
parameters of the transponder under test, than are required by Federal Aviation
Regulation (FAR) 43, Appendix F . Ramp test set operating instructions provides charts,
distance limitations and required airplane antenna configurations for satisfactory ramp
test set results. It is recommended that the ramp test set operator have the most
current operating instructions for the ramp test set and be familiar with its operation
when determining the acceptability of transponder results and compliance with FAR
43, Appendix F .
NOTE: Refer to the TR-220 Operating Manual for detailed information on setup, test screens,
and interpreting results of the tests.
NOTE: Refer to the IFR-6000 Operation Manual for information on the UC-584 universal
transponder antenna coupler, COM-18775.
(a) Connect the test set antenna, or antenna coupler, coax connector to the test set
ANTENNA connector.
NOTE: You can use the direct cable connection procedure to perform this test. If you do
the direct cable connection, follow the instructions in the ramp test set Operating
Manual.
(b) Put the TEST SET switch in the ON position.
1) The test set will display a startup screen, then do a self test.
a) Make sure that the display indicates SELF TEST PASS.
(c) Turn the UUT FUNCTION switch on the test set to the XPDR position.
1) The test set will determine the transponder type and display the correct Start Page.

7. ATC System - System Test (With the AVX-10K Test Set)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
WARNING
USE AN ANTENNA COUPLER WITH THE RAMP TESTER TO SIMULATE AN
AIR MODE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THE AIRPLANE WILL TRANSMIT
ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIRCRAFT IN
THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE
TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
AIRCRAFT .
(1) This system test is a full check of the Air Traffic Control (ATC) system. The system test first
does the ATC - Operational Test and then uses the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, to
examine the left and right ATC systems.
(2) The XPDR Mode of the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, provides flight line test capability
for the Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS), Mode S transponders. The auto
test satisfies the 24 month ATC transponder maintenance check requirements.
(3) The AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, can also test airplanes with Automatic Dependent
Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B) function for DO 260, DO 260A, and DO 260B compliant
transponders. The ADS-B tests are not included with the AUTO TEST . These tests satisfy the
ADS-B Out 24 month ATC transponder maintenance check requirements.
(4) Details of individual tests conducted during the AUTO TEST can be stored as files on the
AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186. Tests can be run individually by opening the associated
ribbon prior to running the test.
(5) Different classes of transponders are tested to built-in test limits by selection of configuration
files. If the class of transponder is unknown, generic configuration files are provided for
ATCRBS and Mode S transponders that apply the widest system limits.
(6) Mode S Transponder level is automatically determined when running a test.
(7) The test is applicable to the left and the right ATC system. Set the transponder select switch on
the ATC control panel to the applicable position to do a test of that system.
(8) This Predictive Maintenance & Enhanced Troubleshooting (PMET) procedure is optional and
the results are for evaluation purposes only. No action is required as a result of this procedure
if a flight deck effect or other observed fault does not exist. The recommendations are made to
show Boeing's best practices to make sure that maximum aircraft reliability is reached. If a
flight deck effect or other observed fault exists, it must be corrected with accepted procedures.
34-53-00

F . ATC System Test
SUBTASK 34-53-00-730-041
(1) Do the ATC System Test:
NOTE: When first powered-up, the Test Set displays blank data fields. The last test results are
displayed while Test Set remains powered on.
(a) Click the Top or Bottom tabs on the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, to return to
XPDR Auto Test Screen.
(b) Push the Test Configuration field to show the XPDR CONFIG parameters and select the
desired configuration file.
NOTE: Multiple predefined Configurations are provided to determine the PASS/FAIL
limits applied to ERP , Frequency and MTL measurements. Configurations are
named by class and option. Refer to the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186,
Operation Manual for predefined Configuration details.
NOTE: If the transponder class is not known, select the GENERIC ATCRBS or
GENERIC MODE S configuration file.
(c) To do the Auto Test, push the RUN Soft Key. When the Auto Test completes, a PASS or
FAIL indication is shown at the top of the Auto Test screen.
NOTE: The Auto Test Ribbon is the primary test screen and displays most UUT
parameters requiring user verification.
NOTE: A passed Auto Test complies with the Federal Aviation Regulation (FAR) Part 43
Appendix F test requirements.
(d) Make sure that the Aircraft Address (AA) field shows the correct Mode S Address. Refer
to WDM 34-53-11 or WDM 34-53-21 for the Mode S Address code.
(e) Scroll down to show the complete Auto Test List. Tests may be reviewed or run
individually by opening the desired ribbon prior to pressing the RUN key.
(f) To do the tests individually in the Test List, do these steps:
1) Open only the ribbons for the tests that you want to run.
2) Push the RUN Soft Key.

(4) To do the tests for ADS-B, do the following:
NOTE: This test is for the DO-260B requirements for the ADS-B.
(a) Do the ADS-B test setup.
1) Do the following steps on the Captain or F/O CDU:
a) Push RTE button on the CDU to display page RTE 1.
b) Enter the local airport four letter ICAO code (ex. KDFW) in ORIGIN and DEST
fields.
c) Enter COA1234 in the FLT NO field.
d) Push DEP/ARR key.
e) Push Line Select Key (LSK) 1L - DEP to select local airport from the departure
list.
f) Select any departure procedure (SIDS) from the list on the left of the display.
g) If available, select any transition (TRANS) from the list on the left side of the
display.
h) Push LSK 6R ROUTE to return to RTE 1 page.
i) Push LSK 6R ACTIVATE to activate the flight plan.
j) Push EXEC button to confirm the route activation.
2) Run ADS-B Monitor application on the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, and
press the Setup tab.
3) Repeat the setup procedures from step 11.d) for RF Port, Antenna Settings, Cable
Settings and Coupler Loss.
4) Select Advanced Settings and Position Decode:
NOTE: POS DECODE is for B-Definition Subfield (BDS) 0,5 and BDS 0,6.
a) Set to GLOBAL to use global Compact Position Reporting (CPR) algorithm for
latitude and longitude decoding or simulation.
b) Set to LOCAL to use local CPR algorithm for latitude and longitude decoding
or simulation.
5) Select ADS-B Monitor DF Setting.
a) Set DF17 extended squitters to be generated and then return to main setup
screen by clicking the return arrow key or icon.
6) Select Position Settings and Position Entry Method and set to USER ENTRY .
7) Select Latitude and enter local latitude in degrees, minutes, and seconds.
8) Select Longitude and enter the local longitude in degrees, minutes, and seconds.

3. ATC Antenna with Gasket - Removal
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This procedure is used for the removal of antennas that use Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per
737-SL-20-045.
(a) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do the steps
that follow:
(b) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check.
(c) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the antenna and gasket after their removal.
(d) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the antenna gasket.
1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

Zone Area

material residue to prevent silicone oil contamination on other parts of the

5. ATC Antenna with Gasket - Installation
(Figure 402)
A. This procedure is used for the installation of antennas with Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per
737-SL-20-045.
(1) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do the steps that
follow:
(a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check.
(b) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the antenna and gasket after their removal.
(c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the antenna gasket.
1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

Panel.

1) Make sure that the eight red Light Emitting Diode (LED)s go on for 3 seconds, then
go off.
2) Make sure that the green XPNDR LED goes on and that the eight red LEDs stay off.
(d) Release the TEST pushbutton on the left ATC transponder [1].
1) Make sure that the green XPNDR LED stays on.

1) Make sure that the green LED and the nine red LEDs go on for 3 seconds, then go
off.
2) Make sure that the green TPR LED goes on after 2 seconds and that the nine red
LEDs stay off.

four flights is read and the applicable fault light LED comes on.
1) Make sure that the sequence that follows occurs:
a) All the LEDs come on red for approximately two seconds.
b) The LRU STATUS LED comes on green and the other LEDs remain red for
approximately two seconds.
c) All the LEDs go off for approximately two seconds.
d) The test results are displayed for 30 seconds:
• LRU STATUS LED is green - Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) with no fails
• LRU STATUS LED is red - LRU failure
• All the other LEDs are off - LRU with no fails
• All the other LEDs are red - LRU failure.
RYR ALL
(i) Set the transponder select switch on the ATC control panel to the 2 position.
RYR 500-999; RYR 013, 014 POST SB 737-34-3369
(j) Push and hold the test switch on the right ATC transponder [1].
1) Make sure that the eight red LEDs go on for 3 seconds, then go off.
2) Make sure that the green XPNDR LED goes on and that the eight red LEDs stay off.
(k) Release the test switch on the right ATC transponder [1].
1) Make sure that the green XPNDR LED stays on.
RYR 006, 007, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169,
174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317,
322-341, 343, 346-416, 447-499; RYR 013, 014 PRE SB 737-34-3369
(l) Push and hold the TEST pushbutton on the right ATC transponder [1].
1) Make sure that the green LED and the nine red LEDs go on for 3 seconds, then go
off.
2) Make sure that the green TPR LED goes on after 2 seconds and that the nine red
LEDs stay off.
(m) Release the TEST pushbutton on the right ATC transponder [1].
1) Make sure that the green TPR LED goes off.
RYR 417-446
(n) Push and release the PUSH TO TEST switch on the right ATC transponder [1].
NOTE: The PUSH TO TEST switch needs to be held for 1.5 seconds.
1) Make sure that the self-test passes and no faults are detected.
34-53-02
RYR 043, 044
(o) Push momentarily and hold the TEST switch on the front panel of the right ATC
transponder [1].
NOTE: Do not hold the TEST switch for more than five seconds. If you hold the TEST
switch for more than five seconds, the non volatile memory fault data for the last
four flights is read and the applicable fault light LED comes on.
1) Make sure that the sequence that follows occurs:
a) All the LEDs come on red for approximately two seconds.
b) The LRU STATUS LED comes on green and the other LEDs remain red for
approximately two seconds.
c) All the LEDs go off for approximately two seconds.
d) The test results are displayed for 30 seconds:
• LRU STATUS LED is green - LRU with no fails
• LRU STATUS LED is red - LRU failure
• All the other LEDs are off - LRU with no fails
• All the other LEDs are red - LRU failure.
RYR ALL
(p) Put the switch for the ATC mode selector to the STBY position on the ATC Control Panel.
SUBTASK 34-53-02-710-001
(2) Do this task: Air Traffic Control System - Operational Test, TASK 34-53-00-710-801.

117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

3. DME Antenna with Gasket Removal
(Figure 402)
A. General
(1) This task is used for the removal of DME antennas that use Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per
737-SL-20-045.
(2) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do thee steps:
(a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check.
(b) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the DME antenna and gasket after their
removal.
(c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the DME antenna
gasket.
1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

A. General

(2) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do these steps:

(b) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the DME antenna and gasket after their
removal.

gasket.

(c) During the first two seconds of the test, the receiver output goes to a fail condition. The
pointer goes out of view and the amber ADF flag shows momentarily.
(d) For the next two seconds, the receiver output goes to an No Computed Data (NCD)
condition. During this time, the amber ADF flag goes out of view and the pointer stays out
of view.
(e) Next, the test display shows and the pointer goes to a test position of 135 degrees from
the heading lubber line until the end of test.
NOTE: For a dual system, the test is the same for each ADF receiver.

(2) Clean the airplane skin (TASK 51-21-00-100-801).
(a) Remove the old sealant from the airplane skin in the Automatic Direction Finder (ADF)
antenna [1] area.
34-57-01
(b) Clean the mating surface with solvent, B00083.
SUBTASK 34-57-01-620-001
(3) If the airplane skin has corrosion or other damage, do these steps:
(a) To remove the corrosion, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Aluminum
and Aluminum Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-801.
(b) Apply a layer of coating, C00064, on the airplane skin in the area where the ADF
antenna [1] touches the skin.
G. ADF Antenna Installation
SUBTASK 34-57-01-420-001
(1) Install the ADF antenna [1].
(a) Apply a thin layer of compound, A00230, to the antenna base.
(b) Apply the Frekote 700-NC non-peelable parting agent, G02497 (preferred), or Frekote
710-NC non-peelable parting agent, G50313 (preferred), or Frekote 44-NC non-peelable
parting agent, G50335 (alternative), or Frekote 48 NC non-peelable parting agent,
G50711 (alternative), to the ADF antenna base.
(c) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, on the new O-ring [2] and O-ring groove.
(d) Install the new O-ring [2] on the ADF antenna [1].
(e) Remove the protective cover from the electrical connecctor [3].
(f) Connect the electrical connecctor [3] to the ADF antenna [1].
(g) Put the ADF antenna [1] into position on the airplane surface.
(h) Lightly tighten the bolts [4] in a diagonal pattern to hold the ADF antenna [1] in the correct
position.
NOTE: Refer to the IPC for the bolt part number.
CAUTION
TIGHTEN THE BOLTS MANUALLY TO THE CORRECT TORQUE VALUE.
OPERATION OF POWER OR AIR TOOLS TO TIGHTEN THE BOLTS CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ADF ANTENNA SURFACE.
(i) Manually tighten the bolts [4] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
(j) Remove the unwanted compound, A00230, from around the edge of the ADF antenna [1].
H. Resistance Measurement (Preferred)
SUBTASK 34-57-01-760-001
(1) Do a check of the electrical continuity between the ADF antenna [1] baseplate and the airplane
skin.
(a) Loosen one bolt [4] from the ADF antenna [1].
(b) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bolt counterbore and the airplane
skin (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less.
(c) If the resistance measurement caused damage, apply the sealant, A02315, or sealant,
A00247, to the damaged area of the airplane skin.
(d) Manually tighten the bolt [4] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).
34-57-01
I. Resistance Measurement (Alternate)
SUBTASK 34-57-01-760-002
(1) Do a check of the electrical continuity from the inside of the airplane between the ADF
antenna [1] baseplate and the airplane skin.
(a) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the ADF antenna [1] baseplate and
the airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less.
(b) If the resistance measurement caused damage, apply the sealant, A02315, or sealant,
A00247, to the damaged area of the airplane skin.
J. Aerodynamic Fillet Seal Installation
SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-001
(1) Fill the bolts [4] counterbores with approximately 0.3 in. (7.6 mm) of cotton plug.
SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-002
(2) Seal all the bolts [4] with sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, until flush with the ADF
antenna [1] surface (TASK 51-31-00-390-805).
SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-003
(3) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, around the base of the ADF
antenna [1] (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).
NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until
next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of
the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043).
SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-004
(4) Use the hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810, to make a smooth 45-degree
bead.
SUBTASK 34-57-01-140-002
(5) Remove unwanted sealant from the area around the ADF antenna [1] base.
SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-005
(6) Let the sealant dry for the correct cure time.

GPS satellites.

Reference Title

211 Flight Compartment - Left

D. Global Positioning System System Test
SUBTASK 34-58-00-580-002
(1) Move the airplane to a position where the GPS antennas have a clear view of the GPS
satellites, do this task: Maintenance Towing, TASK 09-11-00-580-801.
SUBTASK 34-58-00-860-004
(2) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1

Row Col Number Name
A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2

(3) Do these steps to see the GPS position on the CDU:
(a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU.
(b) Make sure that the steps that follow occur:
1) The time on the CDU agrees with the known time.
2) The date on the CDU agrees with the known date.
(c) Push the line select key (LSK) that is adjacent to <INDEX.
(d) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <POS.
(e) Push the NEXT PAGE key on the CDU.

34-58-00
1) The GPS L position on the CDU agrees with the known airplane position.
NOTE: As much as 5 minutes of time can be necessary for the positions to show

2) The GPS R position on the CDU agrees with the known airplane position.
NOTE: As much as 5 minutes of time can be necessary for the positions to show
on the CDU.
SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-003
(4) Do these steps to do a check of the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU (P5 panel):
(a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1
1) Make sure that the GPS L position goes out of view on the CDU.
2) Make sure that the GPS R position stays in view on the CDU.
3) Make sure that the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU (P5) stays off.
(b) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2
1) Make sure that the GPS R position goes out of view on the CDU.
2) Make sure that the GPS L position stays out of view on the CDU.
3) Make sure that the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU (P5) comes on after
approximately 10 seconds.
(c) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1
Row Col Number Name
A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2
(d) Make sure that the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU goes off.
(e) Stop for approximately 5 minutes until the GPS L and GPS R positions are shown again.
SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-006
(5) Do a check of GPS time and date:

(b) Make sure that the steps that follow occur:

G. GPS Antenna Installation
SUBTASK 34-58-02-390-006
(1) Prepare the GPS antenna [1] as follows:
(a) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, on the new O-ring [4] and the O-ring groove.
(b) Install the O-ring [4] on the GPS antenna [1].
1) Make sure that the O-ring [4] is not damaged and is installed correctly in the o-ring
groove.
(c) Apply a layer of sealant, A00247, on the shank of the screws [2].
SUBTASK 34-58-02-420-004
(2) Install the GPS antenna [1].
(a) Remove the protective covers from the coaxial connector [3].
(b) Examine the coaxial connector [3] for dirt and damage.
(c) Connect the coaxial connector [3].
(d) Tighten the coaxial connector [3] to 8 in-lb (0.9 N·m) - 12 in-lb (1.4 N·m).
34-58-02
(e) Apply a large quantity of silicone compound, D00254, to the outside coaxial connector
and at the exterior connector/antenna interface.
(f) Put the GPS antenna [1] into its position on the airplane.
(g) Install the three screws [2] that hold the GPS antenna [1].
WARNING
DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR
SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT
ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE
THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS,
FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND
FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT .
(h) Remove the unwanted sealant, A00247, from around the antenna with Series 84 solvent,
B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801).
SUBTASK 34-58-02-760-002
(3) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the GPS antenna [1] and airplane skin.
(a) Use an non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614, between the base of the antenna
and airplane skin.
NOTE: You can get access to the base of the antenna through the hole for the last
screw.
1) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less.
SUBTASK 34-58-02-420-005

SUBTASK 34-58-02-390-007
(1) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, around the base of the GPS
antenna [1] (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).
NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until
next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of
the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043).
(a) Apply the sealant all around the edge of the GPS antenna [1].
1) Make sure that no air bubbles are in the sealant.
(b) Use a sufficient quantity of the sealant to permit you to make the surface smooth.

hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).

(3) Remove all the unwanted sealant from the area around the antenna.

34-61-00-470-805FMC Software Installation with a Portable Data LoaderPDF p. 1150

4. FMC Software Installation with a Portable Data Loader
A. General
(1) This procedure tells you how to install software into the Flight Management Computer (FMC)
with a portable data loader.
(a) The FMC usually contains these pieces of software:
1) Operational Program Software (OPS)
2) Navigation Database (NDB)
3) Software Options Database (OPC)
4) Model/Engine Database (MEDB).
(b) The FMC can contain these pieces of optional software:
1) Performance Defaults Database (Perf Defaults)
2) ACARS Datalink Configuration Database (Adaptable Datalink Database (ADDB))
3) Flight Plan Database
34-61-00
4) Loadable Default Data Base (LDDB).
NOTE: When you install a complete set of the FMC software, you should install the OPS first.
Loading the OPS will clear any loaded OPC, NDB, LDDB, and ADDB, therefore, these
programs need to be reloaded.
(2) If you install a full set of the FMC software, you must install the OPS first. The OPS installation
erases all other software installed in the FMC. Also, performance factors that are changed by
manual entry from the Control Display Unit (CDU) go back to their default values.
(a) You must install the NDB and MEDB databases again after the installation of the OPS. If
you do not install the customized OPC, the OPS will use default values.
(b) You must install the optional databases, Perf Defaults or Datalink, again if your airline
uses them. If you do not install a customized Perf Defaults or Datalink database the OPS
will use default values.
(3) If the PDL is connected to the DATA TRANSFER UNIT RECEPTACLE, you cannot use the
ADL to load data.
(4) A Portable Data Loader (PDL) is not a Boeing supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier for
instructions for operation. PDLs have a disk drive for software installation from disks. Some
PDLs have an internal mass storage device. If the software is stored in the PDL, then disks are
not necessary.
(5) The MEDB installation erases the initially installed LDDB. Also the manually selected
performance factors go back to their default values.
(a) You must install the customized LDDB, given directly from the FMC supplier, again if your
airline uses them.
(6) The installation of the OPC, ADDB, LDDB or NDB does not erase other initially installed
software.
(7) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer
are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as
preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders
procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current
capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

NOTE: Because of data loader incompatibility, LOAD COMPLETE may not be shown on

RECORD on line 3 of the FMCS DATA LOADER page increments to the number
shown for TOTAL RECORDS on line 5, then a successful data load occurred.
NOTE: After you eject the diskette from the data loader, the FMC will restart. After the

page shown on the CDU.

CHECK DBL OR INTERFACE - data loader or interface
wiring failure

FMC memory
RESET COUNT EXCEEDED - five load attempts have failed
DB-OFP INCOMPATIBLE - data is not compatible with
the FMC OFP
CHECK MEDIA - a portion of data on the disk
is not able to load
INCORRECT DISK INSERTED - the wrong disk is put in after
INSERT NEXT DISK is shown.

5. FMC Software Crossload
A. General
(1) This procedure tells you how to crossload software from one FMC to the other FMC. A
crossload will install the software into the second FMC significantly faster than the data loader.
(a) The Flight Management Computer (FMC) usually contains these pieces of software:
1) Operational Program Software (OPS)
2) Navigation Database (NDB)
3) Software Options Database (OPC)
4) Model/Engine Database (MEDB).
(b) The FMC can contain these pieces of optional software:
1) Performance Defaults Database (Perf Defaults)
2) ACARS Datalink Configuration Database (Adaptable Datalink Database (ADDB))
3) Flight Plan Database
4) Loadable Default Data Base (LDDB).
(2) If an OP PROGRAM or DATABASE crossload is carried out, all previously entered
performance factors, such as F-F Factor, must be manually entered into the FMC.
(3) If you install a full set of the FMC Software, you must install the OPS first. The OPS installation
erases all other software installed in the FMC. Also, performance factors that are changed by
manual entry from the Control Display Unit (CDU) go back to their default values.
(a) You must install the NDB and MEDB databases again after the installation of the OPS. If
you do not install the customized OPC, the OPS will use default values.
(b) You must install the optional databases, Perf Defaults, Datalink, flight plan or LDDB,
again if your airline uses them. If you do not install a customized Perf Defaults or Datalink
database the OPS will use default values.
(4) The MEDB installation erases the initially installed LDDB. Also, the manually selected
performance factors go back to their default values.
(a) You must install the customized LDDB, given directly from the FMC supplier, again if your
airline uses them.
(5) The installation of the OPC, ADDB, LDDB or NDB does not erase other initially installed
software.
(6) After a dual FMC power-up, the OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page or the DATABASE
CROSSLOAD page is shown automatically on the CDU if the two FMCs have different
software installed.
(7) When the CROSSLOAD> prompt is shown on the FMCS BITE page, you can push the LSK to
manually select the OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page or the DATABASE CROSSLOAD
page.

Zone Area
210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50

C. Procedure
SUBTASK 34-61-00-470-013
(1) Do these steps to crossload the software:
(a) Make sure the CDU shows one of these two pages, the OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD
page or the DATABASE CROSSLOAD page.
NOTE: The CROSSLOAD> prompt is not shown if an FMC is failed, or only one FMC is
powered, or only one FMC is installed in a dual FMC configuration.
NOTE: The OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page lets you install the operational program
and databases into the other FMC. The DATABASE CROSSLOAD page lets you
install only the databases into the other FMC.
NOTE: If the OP PROGRAM INVALID page shows, you must set the FMC source select
switch to the position shown on the CDU.
(b) Push the CDU LSK next to COPY FROM LEFT(RIGHT) to select the FMC you want to
copy from.
NOTE: If you see the message SET FMC SOURCE SELECT TO BOTH-ON-L(R), make
sure the switch is in the correct position.
(c) Push the EXEC key on the CDU.
(d) The CROSSLOAD IN PROGRESS message shows during the FMC crossload.
(e) The CROSSLOAD COMPLETE message shows for a successful crossload.
NOTE: The CROSSLOAD FAIL message is shown if the FMC crossload fails. Possible
causes for a failure are loss of communication between the FMC's, loss of power
to one FMC, or failure of the FMC receiving the data. A second attempt may be
made to do the crossload. Select the INDEX prompt to return to the FMC BITE
page. Then select the CROSSLOAD> prompt to repeat the crossload operation.
NOTE: A database crossload failure causes the NEXT MISMATCH prompt to show with
the CROSSLOAD COMPLETE message. The prompt can also show for
mismatches in the analog input discretes or the performance factors. Select the
NEXT MISMATCH prompt to continue.

6. FMC Software Configuration Check
A. General
(1) This procedure tells you how to check the Flight Management Computer (FMC) software
installation.
(2) You must know the correct part number for the FMC software. For the FMC to be an approved
installation, software with the correct part number must be installed.
34-61-00
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-004
(1) Do these steps to do a software configuration check of the FMC:
RYR 056-063, 067-078, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203,
205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999;
RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 081 POST SB 737-34-2000; AIRPLANES WITH DUAL
FMC
(a) Set the Flight Management Computer System (FMCS) transfer switch to the applicable
position:
1) To check the software for the left FMC, set the FMCS transfer switch to the
NORMAL position.
2) To check the software for the right FMC, set the FMCS transfer switch to the BOTH
ON R position.
RYR ALL
(b) Make sure that the Control Display Unit (CDU) display shows the IDENT 1/2 page.
(c) Do these steps if the IDENT 1/2 page is not shown:
1) Push the INIT/REF key on both CDUs.
2) Push the LSK next to IDENTon both CDUs.
(d) Do a check of the FMC operational program and navigational database software:
1) Make sure that the correct part number for the operational program shows below
OP PROGRAM on the CDU.
2) Make sure that the correct part number for the navigation database shows below
NAV DATA on the CDU.
3) Make sure that the correct date range shows below ACTIVE on the CDU.
(e) Push the NEXT PAGE button on the CDU.
(f) Make sure that the CDU display shows the IDENT 2/2 page.
(g) Do a check of this FMC software:
1) Make sure that the correct part number for the software options database shows
below SW OPTIONS on the CDU.
NOTE: You must install the software options database for the FMC to operate. If
you did not install a software options database the CDU will show
DEFAULT050 below SW OPTIONS.
2) Make sure that the correct part number for the model/engine database shows below
MODEL/ENGINE DATA on the CDU.
NOTE: You must install the model/engine database for the FMC to operate. If
INVALID shows on the CDU, the model/engine database was not installed.
If PROGRAM PIN NOT IN MODEL/ENGINE DATABSE shows, the
model/engine database installed does not match the airframe/engine
program pin configuration.
3) Make sure that the correct part number is shown for any installed optional
databases (Perf Defaults, Datalink, Flight plan or Loadable Default).

7. CDU Software Installation with a Portable Data Loader (AIRPLANES WITH LIQUID CRYSTAL
DISPLAY CDU)
A. General
(1) This procedure tells you how to install software into the CDU with a portable data loader.
(2) A Portable Data Loader (PDL) is not a Boeing supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier for
instructions for operation. PDLs have a disk drive for software installation from disks. Some
PDLs have an internal mass storage device. If the software is stored in the PDL, then disks are
not necessary.
(3) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer
are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as
preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders
procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current
capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

A. General

inch diskette.

C. FMC Diagnostic Data Transfer
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-008
(1) Use the FMCPREP PC software to format the disk or prepare the USB flash drive.
(a) You must make a copy of the FMCPREP software on the root directory of a PC hard
drive.
(b) To format a disk, enter the text that follows on your PC:
> FMCPREP<DRIVE>:<Airline ID
where:
<drive> is the letter "A" or "B" of the PCs 3.5 inch disk drive.
Airline ID> is the name of the airline maintenance site (11 characters maximum).
example: FMCPREP B: Cincinatti
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-009
(2) Make sure the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page shows on the CDU.
(a) If the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page is not shown, do these steps:
1) Push the INIT REF key.
2) Push the LSK adjacent to MAINT> to show the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page.
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-010
(3) Push the LSK adjacent to FMC DOWNLOAD>.
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-023
(4) Follow the directions on the FMC DATA LOADER page.
(a) Select Capt Left System or F/O Right System on Data Load Select switch.
(b) Select FMC on the Data Load System Select switch.
(c) Select FMC Source on the Overhead Source Select Panel.
NOTE: When the FMC Source Select Switch is in the Both On Right Position the
diagnostic data from the F/Os or Right FMC will be downloaded.
34-61-00
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-012
(5) Push the LSK adjacent to CONTINUE.
NOTE: If you push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO EXIT>, the FMC will do a cold start
power-up.
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-028
(6) Remove the media from the drive or port when the download is complete.
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-013
(7) Put the formatted disk into the data loader disk drive.
NOTE: If the disk is write protected, the FMC download will not continue from this page.
Remove the disk and set the write- protected tab to the write position. Put the disk
back into the data loader disk drive.
NOTE: The disk may only contain FMC download data.
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-014
(8) The FMC automatically starts the data transfer sequence.
NOTE: When the data transfer is complete, the FMC DATA LOADER page shows
DOWNLOAD COMPLETE.
SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-015
(9) Remove the disk and push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO EXIT>.
NOTE: If you push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO EXIT>, the FMC will do a cold start
power-up.

2. Flight Management Computer System - Operational Test
A. General
(1) The operational test does a quick check of the flight management computer system. The test
makes sure that the system is serviceable.
(2) You can do the tests in sequence or one at a time. The Prepare For Test steps must be done
before each test or sequence of tests.
RYR 006, 007, 018-020, 043, 044, 081 PRE SB 737-34-2000; RYR 013, 014 PRE SB 737-34-2379 AND PRE SB
737-34-2000; AIRPLANES WITH SINGLE FMC AND CDU
(3) The Control Display Unit (CDU) is necessary for this procedure. You can use CDU No. 1 (Left
or Captain's CDU) or CDU No. 2 (Right or First Officer's CDU) to do this procedure. This
procedure makes reference to the two CDUs to verify their operational integrity.
RYR 043, 044 POST SB 737-23-1484 AND PRE SB 737-34-2000; AIRPLANES WITH SINGLE FMC AND MCDU
(4) The CDU is necessary for this procedure. You can use CDU No. 1 (Left or Captain's CDU) or
CDU No. 2 (Right or First Officer's CDU) to do this procedure. This procedure makes reference
to the two CDUs to verify their operational integrity.

necessary for this procedure. This procedure uses two CDUs to make sure the operational test

FMC).

4. FMCS Performance Factors - Adjustment
A. General
(1) This task gives steps to adjust these performance factors:
(a) Drag factor
(b) F-F factor
34-61-00
(c) Maneuver margin
(d) Minimum cruise time
(e) Minimum rate of climb (climb) margin
(f) Minimum rate of climb (cruise) margin
(g) Minimum rate of climb (engine out) margin.
(2) You can do these adjustments in sequence or one at a time. The Prepare For Adjustment
steps must be done before each adjustment or sequence of adjustments.
NOTE: If a factor has had its entry capability disabled by a loadable performance defaults
database, you cannot change its value using this procedure. You must load a new
performance defaults database with the new factor value.
(3) The Control Display Unit (CDU) is necessary for this procedure. You can use CDU No. 1 or
CDU No. 2 to do this procedure.

SUBTASK 34-61-01-020-001

SUBTASK 34-61-01-140-001
(2) Clean the cooling vent:
(a) Use the vacuum cleaner, COM-2618, to remove blockage from the air inlet and outlet
holes on the Control Display Unit (CDU).
(b) Clean the grills with a paper towel or soft cloth moist with Liqui-Nox detergent, B00673,
and water (TASK 20-30-31-910-801).
(c) Dry the grills with cotton wiper, G00034.
(d) Use the vacuum cleaner, COM-2618, to remove blockage from the air outlet hole below
the Pilot's Forward Electronic Panel (P9).
RYR 006, 007, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,

SUBTASK 34-61-01-100-003
(3) Clean the cooling vents:
(a) Use the vacuum cleaner, COM-2618, to remove blockage from the Liquid Crystal Display
(LCD) backlight cooling vents, top and bottom central chamber cooling vent, and the rear
chamber vent.
(b) Inspect for any loose debris and dust buildup that remains in the vent openings.
(c) If any debris and dust remain in the CDU vent openings, do these steps:
NOTE: The CDU cover panels do not need to be removed for these steps.
1) If it is necessary, use the safety glasses, STD-1137, and filtering facepiece,
STD-1136.
2) Blow pressurized air controlled at 40.0 psi (275.8 kPa) - 90.0 psi (620.5 kPa)
through and around these display unit locations:
a) Rear chamber vent opening.
b) Top and bottom central chamber cooling vent.
<1> For the top vent the air should be blown toward the display unit
keyboard.
34-61-01
RYR 006, 007, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169,

c) LCD backlight cooling vents.
3) Use the vacuum to remove dirt and dust debris.
4) If it is necessary, repeat these cleaning steps.
NOTE: The debris can dislodge and move into other areas of the CDU.
(d) Inspect the LCD backlight cooling vents to make sure they are clear of debris.
NOTE: If significant amounts of debris still remain, this could result in a cooling airflow
blockage and reduced display unit reliability.
NOTE: It is recommended that the unit be returned to the supplier for cleaning if
significant debris remains after this procedure is completed.

C. Procedure
SUBTASK 34-61-01-100-002
(1) Clean the display surface of the FMCS control display unit (CDU) with the Supaspray cleaner,
B50012, and the Supacloth cloth, B50013, or the ALGLAS Visial cleaner, G02457:
(a) Apply 2 or 3 sprays of the Supaspray to the Supacloth, or open the wet sachet.
(b) Use the moist cloth or the wet sachet to clean the display surface in a straight line from
top to bottom.
(c) Gradually move from one side of the display surface to the other side while you clean
from top to bottom.
(d) When the display surface is clean, use a clean, dry area of the cloth or the dry sachet in a
straight line from top to bottom to dry the display surface.

G. FMCS Transfer Relay Installation Test
SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-001
(1) Do these steps for the annunciator test:
(a) Make sure the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH is set to the NORMAL position.
NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on
that CDU.
(b) Push the CLR Key on the CDUs to remove the alert level message from the CDU
scratchpad.
(c) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1
(d) Make sure the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's (P1) and first officer's (P3)
instrument panels come on.
(e) Push the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the autoflight status annunciators (ASAs) and
make sure that the lights go off.
(f) Set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the BOTH ON R position.
NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on
that CDU.
(g) Push the CLR Key on the CDUs to remove the alert level message from the CDU
scratchpad.
(h) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs
are off.
(i) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 16 C01262 FMCS CMPTR 2
34-61-04
(j) Make sure the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs
come on.
(k) Push the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the ASAs and make sure that the lights go
off.
(l) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1
(m) After 15 seconds, set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the BOTH ON L position.
NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on
that CDU.
(n) Push the CLR Key on the CDUs to remove the alert level message from the CDU
scratchpad.
(o) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs
are off.
(p) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 16 C01262 FMCS CMPTR 2
(q) After 15 seconds, set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the NORMAL position.
(r) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs
are still off.
(s) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1
(t) Put the MASTER DIM and TEST switch in the TEST position.
(u) Make sure that the MSG, CALL, FAIL, OFST , and EXEC annunciator lights on the CDUs
come on.
(v) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs
come on.
(w) Push the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the ASAs and make sure that the lights go
off.
(x) Put the MASTER DIM and TEST switch in the DIM position.
(y) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1
H. Operational Program, Navigation Database, and Fixed Outputs Checks
SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-002
(1) If it is necessary, do the “Prepare for Test” steps from Flight Management Computer System -
Operational Test, TASK 34-61-00-710-801.
34-61-04
SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-003
(2) Do these steps to examine the operational program and navigation database:
(a) Set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the BOTH ON L position.
(b) Push the INIT REF key on the two CDUs.
(c) Push the line select key (LSK) adjacent to INDEX on the two CDUs.
(d) Push the LSK adjacent to IDENTon the two CDUs.
(e) Make sure the two CDUs show the IDENT 1/X page.
(f) Make sure the part number of the OP PROGRAM is correct on the two CDUs.
NOTE: The applicable airline department has the correct part number for the OP
PROGRAM.
1) If the OP PROGRAM is incorrect, do this task: FMC Software Installation with a
Portable Data Loader, TASK 34-61-00-470-805.
(g) Make sure the part number of the NAV DATA is correct on the CDU.
NOTE: The applicable airline department has the correct part number for the NAV DATA.
1) If the NAV DATA is incorrect, do this task: FMC Software Installation with a Portable
Data Loader, TASK 34-61-00-470-805.
(h) Make sure the date of the NAV DATA is correct on the two CDUs.
NOTE: You can find the dates for the active navigation database below ACTIVE.
SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-004
(3) Do these steps to do a test of the FMCS fixed outputs.
(a) Make sure that the captain's and first officer's MAIN PANEL CDUs switches are set to
NORM.
(b) Make sure that the captain's and first officer's LOWER CDUs switches are set to NORM.
(c) Select MAP mode on the captain's and first officer's EFIS control panels.
(d) Set the N1 SET switch to AUTO.
(e) Make sure that the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH is set to NORMAL.
(f) Push the INIT REF key on the two CDUs.
(g) Push the line select key (LSK) adjacent to INDEX on the two CDUs.
(h) Push the LSK adjacent to MAINTon the two CDUs.
(i) Push the LSK adjacent to FMCS on the two CDUs.
(j) Push the LSK adjacent to L FMC on the captain's CDU.
(k) Push the LSK adjacent to R FMC on the first officer's CDU.
(l) Push the LSK adjacent to FIXED OUTPUTS on the two CDUs.
(m) Make sure that the captain's and first officer's EFIS display shows "FMC INTERFACE
OK".
(n) Make sure that the OFST , FAIL, and MSG annunciator lights on the two CDUs come on.
(o) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the two CDUs come on.
34-61-04
(p) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 16 C01262 FMCS CMPTR 2
(q) Make sure that the thrust mode annunciator on engine format above the N1 display
cycles through these thrust modes: CRZ, CLB, - - -, CON, TO, GA.
(r) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1
Row Col Number Name
D 16 C01262 FMCS CMPTR 2
NOTE: Wait at least 15 seconds after closing the circuit breaker.
(s) Set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to BOTH ON R.
NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on
that CDU.
(t) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1
(u) Push the LSK adjacent to R FMC on the first officer's CDU.
(v) Push the LSK adjacent to FIXED OUTPUTS on the first officer's CDU.
(w) Make sure that the thrust mode annunciator on engine format above the N1 display
cycles through these thrust modes: CRZ, CLB, - - -, CON, TO, GA.
(x) Close this circuit breaker:
CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2
Row Col Number Name
A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1
NOTE: Wait at least 15 seconds after closing the circuit breaker.
(y) Push the LSK adjacent to INDEX on the first officer's CDU.
(z) Set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to NORMAL.
NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on
